🎀 AgenticMail is available via MCP (mcp__agenticmail__*).

When to reach for it:
  · Building anything that benefits from MULTIPLE specialized roles working in parallel — designer + developer + reviewer, researcher + writer + fact-checker, planner + executor + critic.
  · Coordinating long-running async work that survives across Claude Code restarts (email threads are durable; in-memory state is not).
  · Anywhere you would otherwise spawn the Task tool repeatedly for sub-tasks — prefer AgenticMail when those sub-tasks need to talk to EACH OTHER, not just back to you.

High-leverage tools:
  · mcp__agenticmail__create_account({ name, role })       — spawn a fresh persistent agent identity with its own inbox + API key.
  · mcp__agenticmail__send_email({ to, cc, subject, text, wake }) — kick off the work. CC the whole team; use `wake: ["alice"]` to give exactly one agent the next turn while others stay informed.
  · mcp__agenticmail__call_agent({ agent, message }) / mcp__agenticmail__wait_for_email — blocking RPC when you need a specific answer back before continuing your own turn.

Coordination pattern: one email thread = the shared workspace. Reply-all keeps the audit trail. Use `wake` to control whose turn it is.

Other tools cover: inbox/folder management, drafts, templates, tasks, contacts, signatures, SMS, voice. Full list under mcp__agenticmail__* — discover on demand, don't front-load them all.

- Adopt Effect at the monitor process start boundary while preserving the existing Promise-based tool API.

**Tier: important** — agent-behavior changes across two extensions. Draft PR: https://github.com/valkyriweb/my-pi/pull/85 (worktree `feat-bash-sleep-block-monitor-parity`, 2 commits).

**1. Foreground-sleep block** (`extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts`)
- `assertNoForegroundSleep` in the bash `prepareArguments` wrapper — leading `sleep N` (bare or `&&`/`;`-chained) throws exactly CC's message: `Blocked: sleep 60 followed by: gh pr checks 83. To wait for a condition, use monitor_start with an until-loop…`
- Exempt: `run_in_background: true`, and non-leading sleeps (`until <check>; do sleep 2; done`).
- Bash description gains the proactive nudge sentence (one-time cache rebaseline, byte-stable after).

**2. Monitor → CC parity** (`extensions/monitor/index.ts`) — I pulled CC's actual Monitor schema from this harness as ground truth:
- `triggerOnOutput` now **defaults true** + 200ms wake batching (was off / 2s). ⚠️ This reverses the default you set after the "waited for background terminal" ping-pong — CC's cure is different: tight filters (now demanded in the description) + the wake cap now **stops** the monitor with a "restart with a tighter filter" steer instead of silently muting.
- stderr logs to file/preview but never wakes (CC: stdout is the event stream; `2>&1` to opt in).
- New `persistent: true` — no runtime cap, session-length watches.
- `monitor_start` description ports CC's decision guide: one notification → Bash `run_in_background` + until-loop; one-per-occurrence → monitor; `--line-buffered`/`fflush()` gotchas; "silence is not success" failure-signature coverage.

**Gates**: both smoke tests (incl. new block + live-spawn parity assertions), deferred-tool contracts (41), both typechecks, pre-commit profile/cache checks — all green.

**Pre-existing, not mine**: `test:prompt-health:live` fails at 37.6k tokens vs the 34k soft cap *on main checkout too* — prompt has drifted ~3.6k since the 2026-05-30 rebaseline. Wants a separate triage/rebaseline decision.

`wt done` when you're happy with the default-flip tradeoff.

content.content:
1	# Monitor Extension
2	
3	A pi extension that mirrors Claude Code's `Monitor` tool. Lets the agent start
4	long-running shell processes whose stdout/stderr lines are streamed back as
5	notifications — replacing token-wasting polling/looping (`bash | sleep | cat`).
6	
7	## When to use this vs `bash run_in_background`
8	
9	Pi's `bash` tool has `run_in_background: true`, plus `bash_output` and
10	`bash_kill` siblings. Use that family for work you will check later. Use monitor
11	when output or exit should wake the agent.
12	
13	| Situation | Use |
14	|---|---|
15	| Long build/test/install where no live reaction is needed | `bash({ run_in_background: true })` → one later `bash_output(bgId)` |
16	| Dev server, log tail, file watcher, queue worker | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: false, triggerOnExit: false })` unless errors should wake the agent |
17	| CI/status polling, error watcher, readiness probe | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: true, triggerOnExit: true, maxRuntimeSeconds })` |
18	| Command where only completion matters, but you want an automatic wake | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: false, triggerOnExit: true })` |
19	| Stop the background job | `bash_kill` for bash bg, `monitor_stop` for monitors |
20	
21	The bash family does **not** wake the agent — output sits in a log file under
22	`~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log` until pulled. The monitor family can wake the
23	agent on output batches (`triggerOnOutput`) and/or process exit (`triggerOnExit`).
24	
25	## Tools the agent gets
26	
27	The five `monitor_*` tools are registered by the monitor extension and kept
28	active by the tool-search config when installed:
29	
30	- `monitor_start({ command, description, cwd?, triggerOnOutput?, triggerOnExit?, maxWakeups?, maxRuntimeSeconds? })` → returns a `monitorId`.
31	  Stdout/stderr is saved to `~/.pi/agent/monitor-logs/` and shown as compact UI notifications.
32	  If `pi-goal` is also loaded and the monitor has `triggerOnExit: true`, the active goal waits on that monitor instead of auto-continuing until exit.
33	  Output does **not** wake/steer the model by default. Set `triggerOnOutput: true` only when the agent must react immediately to matching output, CI changes, errors, or watcher events.
34	  Output wakeups are capped (`maxWakeups`, default 20, max 100); after the cap, logging continues but model wakes stop.
35	  Runtime is capped (`maxRuntimeSeconds`, default 3600, max 43200) so abandoned watches do not run forever.
36	  Exit wakes the model by default for task-completion monitors; set `triggerOnExit: false` for pure tails or servers expected to run until stopped.
37	- `monitor_status({ monitorId, tailLines? })` — inspect status + a small buffered tail preview (default 10 lines, hard max 40).
38	- `monitor_read({ monitorId, mode?, maxLines? })` — read a bounded slice from the full saved log (default tail 100 lines, hard max 1000). Prefer shell `rg`/`tail` against `logPath` for narrower searches.
39	- `monitor_stop({ monitorId })` — SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 3s.
40	- `monitor_list()` — list all monitors.
41	
42	The `/monitors` command and `alt+shift+m` shortcut also implicitly activate
43	the toolset (since opening the dialog implies you care about monitoring).
44	Use `/monitors disable` to put them back to sleep mid-session.
45	
46	## What you (the user) see
47	
48	- **Footer status** when ≥1 monitor is active:
49	  `● 2 monitors · ↓ or alt+shift+m`
50	- **`/monitors`** command — opens the monitors dialog (and enables the
51	  agent-facing tools). `/monitors disable` lazy-unloads them; `/monitors enable`
52	  forces them on without opening the dialog.
53	- **alt+shift+m** — same.
54	- **↓ on an empty editor** — opens the dialog.
55	- **Esc on an empty editor** (with running monitors) — stops the most recent
56	  monitor instead of aborting the agent.
57	- In the dialog: `↑↓` select · `enter` view detail · `x` kill · `esc` close.
58	
59	## Install
60	
61	It's already installed (you're reading the README in
62	`~/.pi/agent/extensions/monitor/`). Pi auto-discovers `*/index.ts` under
63	`~/.pi/agent/extensions/`. Restart pi (or `/reload`) to pick it up.
64	
65	## Notes / known limitations
66	
67	- **Editor wrapping**: if another extension also installs a custom editor
68	  (vim mode, etc.), the monitor extension defers to it — meaning ↓/Esc-on-empty
69	  won't intercept. `alt+shift+m` and `/monitors` still work everywhere.
70	- **`onFocus` on `SelectList`**: pressing `x` in the dialog targets the
71	  currently focused row via `SelectList.onFocus`. If your installed
72	  `@valkyriweb/pi-tui` is too old to expose that, `x` falls back to killing
73	  the first row.
74	- **Output truncation / token safety**: output batches are saved to `~/.pi/agent/monitor-logs/<monitorId>.log`; model-facing notifications include only bounded tails when `triggerOnOutput` is enabled. `monitor_status` is capped to a 40-line preview and reports line/byte counts plus wakeup usage. Use `monitor_read` or shell `rg`/`tail` against the logged path when more is genuinely needed.
75	- **Wakeup and runtime caps**: `triggerOnOutput` cannot wake the model forever. The default `maxWakeups` is 20; after that, the monitor keeps logging but stops steering. The default `maxRuntimeSeconds` is 3600; timeout stops the process group and optionally wakes on exit.
76	- **No polling contract**: agents should not repeatedly call `monitor_status`, `monitor_read`, `bash_output`, or `sleep` while a job is running. Use `triggerOnOutput` / `triggerOnExit` to wake the agent, then inspect once.
77	
78	## Canonical examples
79	
80	### Dev server / log tail, inspect manually
81	
82	```ts
83	monitor_start({
84	  command: "npm run dev",
85	  description: "vite dev server",
86	  triggerOnOutput: false,
87	  triggerOnExit: false,
88	  maxRuntimeSeconds: 7200
89	})
90	```
91	
92	### CI/status polling, wake on changes
93	
94	```ts
95	monitor_start({
96	  command: "while gh run view --json status,conclusion; do sleep 30; done",
97	  description: "poll GitHub Actions",
98	  triggerOnOutput: true,
99	  triggerOnExit: true,
100	  maxRuntimeSeconds: 1800,
101	  maxWakeups: 20
102	})
103	```
104	
105	### Completion-only wake
106	
107	```ts
108	monitor_start({
109	  command: "npm test",
110	  description: "test suite completion",
111	  triggerOnOutput: false,
112	  triggerOnExit: true,
113	  maxRuntimeSeconds: 1200
114	})
115	```
116	
117	If no wake is needed, prefer `bash({ command: "npm test", run_in_background: true })` and check once later with `bash_output(bgId)`.
118

125	> stdout line is a notification). For one-shot 'wait until done,' use Bash
126	> with `run_in_background` instead."

# Monitor Extension

A pi extension that mirrors Claude Code's `Monitor` tool. Lets the agent start
long-running shell processes whose stdout/stderr lines are streamed back as
notifications — replacing token-wasting polling/looping (`bash | sleep | cat`).

## When to use this vs `bash run_in_background`

Pi's `bash` tool has `run_in_background: true`, plus `bash_output` and
`bash_kill` siblings. Use that family for work you will check later. Use monitor
when output or exit should wake the agent.

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Long build/test/install where no live reaction is needed | `bash({ run_in_background: true })` → one later `bash_output(bgId)` |
| Dev server, log tail, file watcher, queue worker | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: false, triggerOnExit: false })` unless errors should wake the agent |
| CI/status polling, error watcher, readiness probe | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: true, triggerOnExit: true, maxRuntimeSeconds })` |
| Command where only completion matters, but you want an automatic wake | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: false, triggerOnExit: true })` |
| Stop the background job | `bash_kill` for bash bg, `monitor_stop` for monitors |

The bash family does **not** wake the agent — output sits in a log file under
`~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log` until pulled. The monitor family can wake the
agent on output batches (`triggerOnOutput`) and/or process exit (`triggerOnExit`).

## Tools the agent gets

The five `monitor_*` tools are registered by the monitor extension and kept
active by the tool-search config when installed:

- `monitor_start({ command, description, cwd?, triggerOnOutput?, triggerOnExit?, maxWakeups?, maxRuntimeSeconds? })` → returns a `monitorId`.
  Stdout/stderr is saved to `~/.pi/agent/monitor-logs/` and shown as compact UI notifications.
  If `pi-goal` is also loaded and the monitor has `triggerOnExit: true`, the active goal waits on that monitor instead of auto-continuing until exit.
  Output does **not** wake/steer the model by default. Set `triggerOnOutput: true` only when the agent must react immediately to matching output, CI changes, errors, or watcher events.
  Output wakeups are capped (`maxWakeups`, default 20, max 100); after the cap, logging continues but model wakes stop.
  Runtime is capped (`maxRuntimeSeconds`, default 3600, max 43200) so abandoned watches do not run forever.

# Monitor Extension

A pi extension that mirrors Claude Code's `Monitor` tool. Lets the agent start
long-running shell processes whose stdout lines are streamed back as
notifications (stderr is logged but never wakes) — replacing token-wasting
polling/looping (`bash | sleep | cat`).

## When to use this vs `bash run_in_background`

Pi's `bash` tool has `run_in_background: true`, plus `bash_output` and
`bash_kill` siblings. Use that family for work you will check later. Use monitor
when output or exit should wake the agent.

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Long build/test/install where no live reaction is needed | `bash({ run_in_background: true })` → one later `bash_output(bgId)` |
| One notification when a condition holds ("tell me when CI is green") | `bash({ command: "until <check>; do sleep 2; done", run_in_background: true })` — foreground `sleep` chains are blocked by native-tool-overrides |
| Dev server, log tail, queue worker you inspect manually | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: false, triggerOnExit: false })` |
| One wake per occurrence (errors, CI step results, watcher events) | `monitor_start({ command: "<emits one filtered line per event>" })` — output wakes are the default |
| Session-length watch (PR monitoring, log tail) | `monitor_start({ persistent: true })` — no runtime cap, stop with `monitor_stop` |
| Command where only completion matters, but you want an automatic wake | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: false, triggerOnExit: true })` |
| Stop the background job | `bash_kill` for bash bg, `monitor_stop` for monitors |

The bash family does **not** wake the agent — output sits in a log file under
`~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log` until pulled. The monitor family can wake the
agent on output batches (`triggerOnOutput`) and/or process exit (`triggerOnExit`).

## Tools the agent gets

The five `monitor_*` tools are registered by the monitor extension and kept
active by the tool-search config when installed:

- `monitor_start({ command, description, cwd?, triggerOnOutput?, triggerOnExit?, maxWakeups?, maxRuntimeSeconds? })` → returns a `monitorId`.
  Stdout/stderr is saved to `~/.pi/agent/monitor-logs/` and shown as compact UI notifications.
  If `pi-goal` is also loaded and the monitor has `triggerOnExit: true`, the active goal waits on that monitor instead of auto-continuing until exit.
  Output does **not** wake/steer the model by default. Set `triggerOnOutput: true` only when the agent must react immediately to matching output, CI changes, errors, or watcher events.
  Output wakeups are capped (`maxWakeups`, default 20, max 100); after the cap, logging continues but model wakes stop.
  Runtime is capped (`maxRuntimeSeconds`, default 3600, max 43200) so abandoned watches do not run forever.
  Exit wakes the model by default for task-completion monitors; set `triggerOnExit: false` for pure tails or servers expected to run until stopped.
- `monitor_status({ monitorId, tailLines? })` — inspect status + a small buffered tail preview (default 10 lines, hard max 40).
- `monitor_read({ monitorId, mode?, maxLines? })` — read a bounded slice from the full saved log (default tail 100 lines, hard max 1000). Prefer shell `rg`/`tail` against `logPath` for narrower searches.
- `monitor_stop({ monitorId })` — SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 3s.
- `monitor_list()` — list all monitors.

The `/monitors` command and `alt+shift+m` shortcut also implicitly activate
the toolset (since opening the dialog implies you care about monitoring).
Use `/monitors disable` to put them back to sleep mid-session.

## What you (the user) see

- **Footer status** when ≥1 monitor is active:
  `● 2 monitors · ↓ or alt+shift+m`
- **`/monitors`** command — opens the monitors dialog (and enables the
  agent-facing tools). `/monitors disable` lazy-unloads them; `/monitors enable`
  forces them on without opening the dialog.
- **alt+shift+m** — same.
- **↓ on an empty editor** — opens the dialog.
- **Esc on an empty editor** (with running monitors) — stops the most recent
  monitor instead of aborting the agent.
- In the dialog: `↑↓` select · `enter` view detail · `x` kill · `esc` close.

## Install

It's already installed (you're reading the README in
`~/.pi/agent/extensions/monitor/`). Pi auto-discovers `*/index.ts` under
`~/.pi/agent/extensions/`. Restart pi (or `/reload`) to pick it up.

## Notes / known limitations

- **Editor wrapping**: if another extension also installs a custom editor
  (vim mode, etc.), the monitor extension defers to it — meaning ↓/Esc-on-empty
  won't intercept. `alt+shift+m` and `/monitors` still work everywhere.
- **`onFocus` on `SelectList`**: pressing `x` in the dialog targets the
  currently focused row via `SelectList.onFocus`. If your installed
  `@valkyriweb/pi-tui` is too old to expose that, `x` falls back to killing
  the first row.
- **Output truncation / token safety**: output batches are saved to `~/.pi/agent/monitor-logs/<monitorId>.log`; model-facing notifications include only bounded tails when `triggerOnOutput` is enabled. `monitor_status` is capped to a 40-line preview and reports line/byte counts plus wakeup usage. Use `monitor_read` or shell `rg`/`tail` against the logged path when more is genuinely needed.

file.content:
# Monitor Extension

A pi extension that mirrors Claude Code's `Monitor` tool. Lets the agent start
long-running shell processes whose stdout lines are streamed back as
notifications (stderr is logged but never wakes) — replacing token-wasting
polling/looping (`bash | sleep | cat`).

## When to use this vs `bash run_in_background`

Pi's `bash` tool has `run_in_background: true`, plus `bash_output` and
`bash_kill` siblings. Use that family for work you will check later. Use monitor
when output or exit should wake the agent.

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Long build/test/install where no live reaction is needed | `bash({ run_in_background: true })` → one later `bash_output(bgId)` |
| One notification when a condition holds ("tell me when CI is green") | `bash({ command: "until <check>; do sleep 2; done", run_in_background: true })` — foreground `sleep` chains are blocked by native-tool-overrides |
| Dev server, log tail, queue worker you inspect manually | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: false, triggerOnExit: false })` |
| One wake per occurrence (errors, CI step results, watcher events) | `monitor_start({ command: "<emits one filtered line per event>" })` — output wakes are the default |
| Session-length watch (PR monitoring, log tail) | `monitor_start({ persistent: true })` — no runtime cap, stop with `monitor_stop` |
| Command where only completion matters, but you want an automatic wake | `monitor_start({ triggerOnOutput: false, triggerOnExit: true })` |
| Stop the background job | `bash_kill` for bash bg, `monitor_stop` for monitors |

The bash family does **not** wake the agent — output sits in a log file under
`~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log` until pulled. The monitor family can wake the
agent on output batches (`triggerOnOutput`) and/or process exit (`triggerOnExit`).

## Tools the agent gets

The five `monitor_*` tools are registered by the monitor extension and kept
active by the tool-search config when installed:

- `monitor_start({ command, description, cwd?, triggerOnOutput?, triggerOnExit?, maxWakeups?, maxRuntimeSeconds?, persistent? })` → returns a `monitorId`.
  Stdout/stderr is saved to `~/.pi/agent/monitor-logs/` and shown as compact UI notifications.
  If `pi-goal` is also loaded and the monitor has `triggerOnExit: true`, the active goal waits on that monitor instead of auto-continuing until exit.
  Output **wakes/steers the model by default** (CC parity: stdout is the event stream; lines within 200ms batch into one notification). Set `triggerOnOutput: false` for noisy streams you will inspect manually.
  Only stdout is the event stream — stderr is logged (and shows in previews) but never wakes; merge with `2>&1` inside the command when failures must reach the filter.
  Output wakeups are capped (`maxWakeups`, default 20, max 100); hitting the cap **stops the monitor** (CC parity) with a steer telling the model to restart with a tighter filter.
  Runtime is capped (`maxRuntimeSeconds`, default 3600, max 43200) so abandoned watches do not run forever; `persistent: true` removes the cap for session-length watches (stopped by `monitor_stop` or session shutdown).
  Exit wakes the model by default for task-completion monitors; set `triggerOnExit: false` for pure tails or servers expected to run until stopped.
- `monitor_status({ monitorId, tailLines? })` — inspect status + a small buffered tail preview (default 10 lines, hard max 40).
- `monitor_read({ monitorId, mode?, maxLines? })` — read a bounded slice from the full saved log (default tail 100 lines, hard max 1000). Prefer shell `rg`/`tail` against `logPath` for narrower searches.
- `monitor_stop({ monitorId })` — SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 3s.
- `monitor_list()` — list all monitors.

The `/monitors` command and `alt+shift+m` shortcut also implicitly activate
the toolset (since opening the dialog implies you care about monitoring).
Use `/monitors disable` to put them back to sleep mid-session.

## What you (the user) see

- **Footer status** when ≥1 monitor is active:
  `● 2 monitors · ↓ or alt+shift+m`
- **`/monitors`** command — opens the monitors dialog (and enables the
  agent-facing tools). `/monitors disable` lazy-unloads them; `/monitors enable`
  forces them on without opening the dialog.
- **alt+shift+m** — same.
- **↓ on an empty editor** — opens the dialog.
- **Esc on an empty editor** (with running monitors) — stops the most recent
  monitor instead of aborting the agent.
- In the dialog: `↑↓` select · `enter` view detail · `x` kill · `esc` close.

## Install

It's already installed (you're reading the README in
`~/.pi/agent/extensions/monitor/`). Pi auto-discovers `*/index.ts` under
`~/.pi/agent/extensions/`. Restart pi (or `/reload`) to pick it up.

## Notes / known limitations

- **Editor wrapping**: if another extension also installs a custom editor
  (vim mode, etc.), the monitor extension defers to it — meaning ↓/Esc-on-empty
  won't intercept. `alt+shift+m` and `/monitors` still work everywhere.
- **`onFocus` on `SelectList`**: pressing `x` in the dialog targets the
  currently focused row via `SelectList.onFocus`. If your installed
  `@valkyriweb/pi-tui` is too old to expose that, `x` falls back to killing
  the first row.
- **Output truncation / token safety**: output batches are saved to `~/.pi/agent/monitor-logs/<monitorId>.log`; model-facing notifications include only bounded tails when `triggerOnOutput` is enabled. `monitor_status` is capped to a 40-line preview and reports line/byte counts plus wakeup usage. Use `monitor_read` or shell `rg`/`tail` against the logged path when more is genuinely needed.
- **Wakeup and runtime caps**: `triggerOnOutput` cannot wake the model forever. The default `maxWakeups` is 20; hitting the cap stops the monitor with a restart-with-a-tighter-filter steer (CC parity — previously it kept logging with wakes muted). The default `maxRuntimeSeconds` is 3600 (skipped under `persistent: true`); timeout stops the process group and optionally wakes on exit.
- **No polling contract**: agents should not repeatedly call `monitor_status`, `monitor_read`, `bash_output`, or `sleep` while a job is running. Use `triggerOnOutput` / `triggerOnExit` to wake the agent, then inspect once.

## Canonical examples

### Dev server / log tail, inspect manually

```ts
monitor_start({
  command: "npm run dev",
  description: "vite dev server",
  triggerOnOutput: false,
  triggerOnExit: false,
  maxRuntimeSeconds: 7200
})
```

### CI/status polling, wake on changes

Output wakes are the default — the work goes into the filter: emit only lines
you would act on, covering failure states too (silence looks identical to
"still running").

```ts
monitor_start({
  command: "while true; do s=$(gh run view --json status,conclusion --jq '.status + \" \" + (.conclusion // \"\")'); [ \"$s\" != \"$prev\" ] && echo \"$s\"; prev=$s; case $s in completed*) break;; esac; sleep 30; done",
  description: "PR CI checks",
  maxRuntimeSeconds: 1800
})
```

### Completion-only wake

```ts
monitor_start({
  command: "npm test",
  description: "test suite completion",
  triggerOnOutput: false,
  triggerOnExit: true,
  maxRuntimeSeconds: 1200
})
```

If no wake is needed, prefer `bash({ command: "npm test", run_in_background: true })` and check once later with `bash_output(bgId)`.

## Reference

`~/Projects/oss/claude-code-cli-src-code/`. Notable strings:

> "Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each
> stdout line is a notification). For one-shot 'wait until done,' use Bash
> with `run_in_background` instead."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Shared auto-compaction threshold for agent harnesses.
if [ -f "$HOME/.pi/agent/token-budget.env" ]; then
  set +u
  . "$HOME/.pi/agent/token-budget.env"
  set -u
  export PI_AUTO_COMPACT_TOKEN_LIMIT CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW
fi

# Source ~/.zshenv to inherit user env (PATH, DREAM_QMD_HTTP_PORT, etc.)
# Warp launches commands via `zsh --no_rcs` which skips all rc files, so Pi
# would otherwise inherit a near-empty environment.
#
# Skip-on-sentinel: when PI_ENV_LOADED=1 is already set, the parent shell
# (or an earlier pi launch in the same shell tree) already sourced it. This
# saves ~60ms on every nested pi launch (intercom-spawned sessions, agent
# subprocesses). Warp/first-launch still pays the cost.
if [ -f "$HOME/.zshenv" ] && [ -z "${PI_ENV_LOADED:-}" ]; then
  set +u
  source "$HOME/.zshenv" 2>/dev/null || true
  set -u
  export PI_ENV_LOADED=1
fi

exec /Users/luke/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/pi "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch a Pi maintenance session to prepare a safe source-checkout update.
# This is intended for settings.sourceUpdateCommand so `pi update` creates an
# update branch and health-checks it instead of mutating the daily main checkout.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
FORK_DIR="${RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR:-$HOME/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork}"
PI_BIN="${RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_AGENT_BIN:-pi}"
UPDATE_BRANCH="${RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_BRANCH:-lue/pi-upstream-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)}"
UPDATE_WORKTREE="${RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_WORKTREE:-$HOME/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update}"
HEALTH_CHECK="${RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_HEALTH_CHECK:-npm run check}"

PROMPT=$(printf '%s\n' \
  "You are a Pi maintenance agent running because Luke typed \`pi update\`." \
  "" \
  "Goal: prepare a safe update branch for Luke's source-checkout Pi installation." \
  "" \
  "Work from this repo unless inspection requires another cwd:" \
  "" \
  "  $FORK_DIR" \
  "" \
  "Update branch:" \
  "" \
  "  $UPDATE_BRANCH" \
  "" \
  "Update worktree:" \
  "" \
  "  $UPDATE_WORKTREE" \
  "" \
  "Health check:" \
  "" \
  "  $HEALTH_CHECK" \
  "" \
  "Rules:" \
  "- Do not ask Luke questions unless the update is blocked by a conflict or destructive choice." \
  "- First inspect git status, branch state, remotes, and worktrees in $FORK_DIR." \
  "- Do not stash, merge into, push to, or otherwise mutate daily main." \
  "- If $FORK_DIR is dirty or not on main, stop and report the exact files/branch." \
  "- Fetch origin and upstream with tags/prune." \
  "- Ensure local main is a clean fast-forward of origin/main only; do not merge upstream into main." \
  "- Create or reuse $UPDATE_BRANCH in $UPDATE_WORKTREE from origin/main." \
  "- Merge upstream/main into $UPDATE_BRANCH inside $UPDATE_WORKTREE." \
  "- Resolve only mechanical merge conflicts. Stop for product choices or cache/tool semantics you cannot prove safe." \
  "- Run the health check in $UPDATE_WORKTREE: $HEALTH_CHECK." \
  "- On success, report branch, worktree, HEAD, health-check result, and the exact PR command for Luke to run if review passes.")

cd "$REPO_ROOT"
"$PI_BIN" \
  --print \
  --tools bash,read,grep,find,ls,edit,write \
  "$PROMPT"
AGENT_EXIT=$?

# Verify the fork/update worktree are in a clean post-update state. The agent
# can exit 0 after reporting an unresolved conflict; without this check, pi's
# caller would then print "Updated pi" despite an in-progress merge/rebase.
verify_no_in_progress_git_operation() {
  local repo_dir="$1"

  if [[ ! -d "$repo_dir" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi

  local git_dir_path
  git_dir_path="$(git -C "$repo_dir" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null || echo "$repo_dir/.git")"
  if [[ -e "$git_dir_path/MERGE_HEAD" ]]; then
    echo "error: merge in progress in $repo_dir; resolve before rerunning pi update" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if [[ -d "$git_dir_path/rebase-merge" || -d "$git_dir_path/rebase-apply" ]]; then
    echo "error: rebase in progress in $repo_dir; resolve before rerunning pi update" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_dir" ls-files --unmerged | grep -q .; then
    echo "error: unmerged paths remain in $repo_dir" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

verify_no_in_progress_git_operation "$FORK_DIR"
verify_no_in_progress_git_operation "$UPDATE_WORKTREE"

exit "$AGENT_EXIT"

# Changelog

All notable changes to `claude-bridge` are documented here.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Releases are cut by pushing a `vX.Y.Z` (stable) or `vX.Y.Z-beta.N` (beta) git
tag, which triggers `.github/workflows/release.yml`. The tag version must match
`package.json`. See [docs/pi-runtime-release-strategy.md](https://github.com/valkyriweb/pi-claude-bridge)
in `my-pi` for the channel model.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- Fixed rolling prompt-cache marker placement for long Pi edit-loop conversations. OAuth system wrapping now keeps the stable system marker but stops spending a second marker on the dynamic system tail once real conversation history exists, preserving Anthropic's 4-marker budget for tools plus two rolling transcript markers. This prevents sessions from pinning `cache_read` at the system/tools anchor and rewriting the growing transcript tail every turn after resume/tool-schema changes.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-05-31

7	---

10	
11	| # | Runtime | Host | Service | Source of truth | Smoke endpoint |
12	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
13	| **A3** | MacBook local bridge | `lukes-macbook-pro` | launchd `com.pi.claude-bridge` | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` working tree | `curl http://127.0.0.1:9100/health` |
14	| **B1** | Mac Mini local bridge | `luke-and-naddy-server` | launchd `com.pi.claude-bridge` | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` working tree (mirrored) | `curl http://127.0.0.1:9100/health` (over tailnet ssh) |
15	| **C1** | lue-kube cluster bridge | k8s deploy `claude-bridge/claude-bridge` pinned to `lue-and-naddy-kube` | `ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:<TAG>@sha256:<digest>` | `~/Projects/infra/lue-kube/k3s/apps/claude-bridge/base/app.yaml` (image tag) + `docker/claude-bridge/Dockerfile` build pulls pi-claude-bridge `CLAUDE_BRIDGE_REF` | `kubectl -n claude-bridge exec deploy/claude-bridge -- curl -s localhost:9100/health` |
16	
17	**Consumers** (do **not** run a bridge; they route through C1 via cluster DNS `claude-bridge.claude-bridge.svc.cluster.local:9100`):
18	
19	- **paperclip pod** (`paperclip/paperclip-otel`) — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=…/source/paperclip`
20	- **multica-runtime pod** (`multica/multica-runtime`) — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=…/source/multica`
21	- **multica-runtime-lue** external worker — same image surface, same egress
22	- Any MacBook CLI (Claude Code, Codex, pi) — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=…/source/macbook` → A3
23	
24	A change to bridge behavior is live for all consumers as soon as their fronting bridge restarts. No per-consumer rollout needed; **just bounce the bridge they dial**.
25	
26	**Not bridge hosts (common confusables):**
27	
28	- `core-wholesale-opik` — Opik backend, consumes spans, no bridge.
29	- `pi-sidecar` in `bermont-kube/horizon` — naming collision; Laravel AI sidecar, not pi-mono-fork.
30	- `old-15-mbp` / archived MacBooks — not in current runtime set.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Rollout procedure
35	
36	### 0. Land the change
37	
38	```bash
39	git -C ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge commit -am "<change>"
40	npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge test
41	git -C ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge push
42	```
43	
44	Note the short SHA — every downstream step keys off it.
45	
46	### 1. A3 — MacBook
47	
48	```bash
49	launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.pi.claude-bridge
50	sleep 2
51	curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9100/health | jq .
52	# Then a real round-trip with the affected behavior, e.g.:
53	curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9100/v1/messages \
54	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
55	  -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","max_tokens":40,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"smoke"}]}' \
56	  | jq '{model, stop_reason, in: .usage.input_tokens, out: .usage.output_tokens}'
57	```
58	
59	### 2. B1 — Mac Mini
60	
61	Mac Mini has no `tmux` on the login PATH (it's at `/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux`). Use a script + scp pattern to avoid quoting hell:
62	
63	```bash
64	cat > /tmp/mini-bridge-update.sh <<'EOF'
65	#!/bin/bash
66	set -e
67	cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge
68	git pull --ff-only
69	launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.pi.claude-bridge
70	sleep 3
71	curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9100/health > /tmp/bridge-health.json
72	curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9100/v1/messages \
73	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
74	  -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","max_tokens":40,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"smoke"}]}' \
75	  > /tmp/bridge-smoke.json
76	EOF
77	scp /tmp/mini-bridge-update.sh luke@luke-and-naddy-server:/tmp/
78	ssh luke@luke-and-naddy-server '/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux new-session -d -s bridge-update "bash /tmp/mini-bridge-update.sh > /tmp/bridge-update.log 2>&1"'
79	sleep 12
80	ssh luke@luke-and-naddy-server 'cat /tmp/bridge-update.log; echo ---; cat /tmp/bridge-health.json; echo; cat /tmp/bridge-smoke.json'
81	```
82	
83	If the Mini has uncommitted local changes (it has historically), `git pull --ff-only` fails. Inspect with `git -C ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge status` over ssh — stash with a labelled name (`pre-<change>-rollout-YYYY-MM-DD`) only after confirming it's not a divergence you want to keep.
84	
85	### 3. C1 — lue-kube cluster
86	
87	Build the image, push to ghcr, update the manifest, let Flux apply.
88	
89	```bash
90	REF=$(git -C ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge rev-parse --short HEAD)
91	TAG="$(date +%Y.%m.%d).${REF}"
92	gh auth token > /tmp/.gh-token-build
93	
94	docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 \
95	  --build-arg CLAUDE_BRIDGE_REF="${REF}" \
96	  --secret id=gh-token,src=/tmp/.gh-token-build \
97	  -t "ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:${TAG}" \
98	  -f docker/claude-bridge/Dockerfile \
99	  --push ~/Projects/infra/lue-kube
100	
101	rm -f /tmp/.gh-token-build
102	
103	DIGEST=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:${TAG}" --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}')
104	echo "Image: ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:${TAG}@${DIGEST}"
105	```
106	
107	Then update `~/Projects/infra/lue-kube/k3s/apps/claude-bridge/base/app.yaml` — the `image:` line — commit + PR + merge. Flux on the cluster picks it up; or `flux reconcile kustomization apps -n flux-system` to force.
108	
109	Smoke after rollout:
110	
111	```bash
112	kubectl -n claude-bridge rollout status deploy/claude-bridge
113	kubectl -n claude-bridge exec deploy/claude-bridge -- sh -c \
114	  'curl -s localhost:9100/health; echo; curl -s -X POST localhost:9100/source/test/v1/messages \
115	     -H "content-type: application/json" -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
116	     -d "{\"model\":\"claude-opus-4-8\",\"max_tokens\":40,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"smoke\"}]}"'
117	```
118	
119	A 200 with a populated `usage` block confirms paperclip + multica will see the new behavior on their next request.
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Verification matrix
124	
125	| # | Check | What "pass" looks like |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| A3 | `curl 127.0.0.1:9100/health` | `{"status":"ok","auth":"keychain",...}` |
128	| A3 | round-trip with new behavior | 200, expected `usage` / headers / response shape |
129	| B1 | same, over tailnet | `auth:"static"` (Mini runs static OAuth) |
130	| C1 | `kubectl rollout status` | `successfully rolled out` |
131	| C1 | in-pod `/source/test/v1/messages` | 200 from Anthropic with `usage` block |
132	| All | Opik dashboard, project `claude-bridge` | new spans tagged `bridge.source=macbook|paperclip|multica` within 1–2 min |
133	
134	If C1 smoke fails but the rollout succeeded, check sealed-secret `claude-bridge-auth` — the static OAuth token may have expired (1y validity; tracked in 1Password Personal / `<persona> setup-token`).
135	
136	---

# claude-bridge rollout playbook

How to ship a change in `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` to **every** runtime that fronts an LLM call. Companion to [`pi-stack-inventory.md`](./pi-stack-inventory.md) §1, which is the canonical "where does pi/bridge run" map — this doc is the procedure.

Touch the source once, roll the three runtimes below in order, smoke each. If you skip the cluster, paperclip + multica silently keep running the old code.

---

## Bridge runtimes (every install)

| # | Runtime | Host | Service | Source of truth | Smoke endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A3** | MacBook local bridge | `lukes-macbook-pro` | launchd `com.pi.claude-bridge` | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` working tree | `curl http://127.0.0.1:9100/health` |
| **B1** | Mac Mini local bridge | `luke-and-naddy-server` | launchd `com.pi.claude-bridge` | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` working tree (mirrored) | `curl http://127.0.0.1:9100/health` (over tailnet ssh) |
| **C1** | lue-kube cluster bridge | k8s deploy `claude-bridge/claude-bridge` pinned to `lue-and-naddy-kube` | `ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:<TAG>@sha256:<digest>` | `~/Projects/infra/lue-kube/k3s/apps/claude-bridge/base/app.yaml` (image tag) + `docker/claude-bridge/Dockerfile` build pulls pi-claude-bridge `CLAUDE_BRIDGE_REF` | `kubectl -n claude-bridge exec deploy/claude-bridge -- curl -s localhost:9100/health` |

**Consumers** (do **not** run a bridge; they route through C1 via cluster DNS `claude-bridge.claude-bridge.svc.cluster.local:9100`):

- **paperclip pod** (`paperclip/paperclip-otel`) — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=…/source/paperclip`
- **multica-runtime pod** (`multica/multica-runtime`) — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=…/source/multica`
- **multica-runtime-lue** external worker — same image surface, same egress
- Any MacBook CLI (Claude Code, Codex, pi) — `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=…/source/macbook` → A3

A change to bridge behavior is live for all consumers as soon as their fronting bridge restarts. No per-consumer rollout needed; **just bounce the bridge they dial**.

**Not bridge hosts (common confusables):**

- `core-wholesale-opik` — Opik backend, consumes spans, no bridge.
- `pi-sidecar` in `bermont-kube/horizon` — naming collision; Laravel AI sidecar, not pi-mono-fork.
- `old-15-mbp` / archived MacBooks — not in current runtime set.

---

## Rollout procedure

### 0. Land the change

```bash
git -C ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge commit -am "<change>"
npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge test
git -C ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge push
```

Note the short SHA — every downstream step keys off it.

### 1. A3 — MacBook

```bash
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.pi.claude-bridge
sleep 2
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9100/health | jq .
# Then a real round-trip with the affected behavior, e.g.:
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9100/v1/messages \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
  -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","max_tokens":40,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"smoke"}]}' \
  | jq '{model, stop_reason, in: .usage.input_tokens, out: .usage.output_tokens}'
```

### 2. B1 — Mac Mini

Mac Mini has no `tmux` on the login PATH (it's at `/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux`). Use a script + scp pattern to avoid quoting hell:

```bash
cat > /tmp/mini-bridge-update.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -e
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge
git pull --ff-only
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.pi.claude-bridge
sleep 3
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9100/health > /tmp/bridge-health.json
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9100/v1/messages \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
  -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","max_tokens":40,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"smoke"}]}' \
  > /tmp/bridge-smoke.json
EOF
scp /tmp/mini-bridge-update.sh luke@luke-and-naddy-server:/tmp/
ssh luke@luke-and-naddy-server '/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux new-session -d -s bridge-update "bash /tmp/mini-bridge-update.sh > /tmp/bridge-update.log 2>&1"'
sleep 12
ssh luke@luke-and-naddy-server 'cat /tmp/bridge-update.log; echo ---; cat /tmp/bridge-health.json; echo; cat /tmp/bridge-smoke.json'
```

If the Mini has uncommitted local changes (it has historically), `git pull --ff-only` fails. Inspect with `git -C ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge status` over ssh — stash with a labelled name (`pre-<change>-rollout-YYYY-MM-DD`) only after confirming it's not a divergence you want to keep.

### 3. C1 — lue-kube cluster

Build the image, push to ghcr, update the manifest, let Flux apply.

```bash
REF=$(git -C ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge rev-parse --short HEAD)
TAG="$(date +%Y.%m.%d).${REF}"
gh auth token > /tmp/.gh-token-build

docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 \
  --build-arg CLAUDE_BRIDGE_REF="${REF}" \
  --secret id=gh-token,src=/tmp/.gh-token-build \
  -t "ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:${TAG}" \
  -f docker/claude-bridge/Dockerfile \
  --push ~/Projects/infra/lue-kube

rm -f /tmp/.gh-token-build

DIGEST=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:${TAG}" --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}')
echo "Image: ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:${TAG}@${DIGEST}"
```

Then update `~/Projects/infra/lue-kube/k3s/apps/claude-bridge/base/app.yaml` — the `image:` line — commit + PR + merge. Flux on the cluster picks it up; or `flux reconcile kustomization apps -n flux-system` to force.

Smoke after rollout:

```bash
kubectl -n claude-bridge rollout status deploy/claude-bridge
kubectl -n claude-bridge exec deploy/claude-bridge -- sh -c \
  'curl -s localhost:9100/health; echo; curl -s -X POST localhost:9100/source/test/v1/messages \
     -H "content-type: application/json" -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
     -d "{\"model\":\"claude-opus-4-8\",\"max_tokens\":40,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"smoke\"}]}"'
```

A 200 with a populated `usage` block confirms paperclip + multica will see the new behavior on their next request.

---

## Verification matrix

| # | Check | What "pass" looks like |
|---|---|---|
| A3 | `curl 127.0.0.1:9100/health` | `{"status":"ok","auth":"keychain",...}` |
| A3 | round-trip with new behavior | 200, expected `usage` / headers / response shape |
| B1 | same, over tailnet | `auth:"static"` (Mini runs static OAuth) |
| C1 | `kubectl rollout status` | `successfully rolled out` |
| C1 | in-pod `/source/test/v1/messages` | 200 from Anthropic with `usage` block |
| All | Opik dashboard, project `claude-bridge` | new spans tagged `bridge.source=macbook|paperclip|multica` within 1–2 min |

If C1 smoke fails but the rollout succeeded, check sealed-secret `claude-bridge-auth` — the static OAuth token may have expired (1y validity; tracked in 1Password Personal / `<persona> setup-token`).

---

## Companion docs

- [`pi-stack-inventory.md`](./pi-stack-inventory.md) — canonical runtime map (every place pi + bridge runs).
- [`cache-strategy.md`](./cache-strategy.md) — bridge cache-marker behavior.

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Session picker badges sessions that are open in another live pi process, backed by a `session-liveness` probe.

### Fixed

- Complete the prompt-cache affinity refactor across two layers. (1) In `agent-session.ts`, the interactive cache-heartbeat and the four model-switch paths were still passing `cwd` to `createPromptCacheAffinityKey`, which now expects the prefix context (`{systemPrompt, tools}`); the stale `cwd` argument collapsed the affinity key to a constant-per-family value (and the tree no longer type-checked). (2) The computed key was then silently dropped one hop before the provider: `packages/ai`'s shared `buildBaseOptions` hand-enumerates which option fields reach the provider request and omitted `cacheAffinityKey`, so every provider (Codex, OpenAI-responses, completions, Anthropic, …) fell back to keying the prompt cache by `sessionId`. With both fixed, all entry paths derive the key from the real prefix shape and it actually reaches the provider — verified at runtime: three independent Codex sessions with the same prefix now emit one shared `pi:openai-codex:codex:…` affinity and one shared shape-derived `prompt_cache_key` (no longer `== sessionId`).
- Record a `model_change` entry when an existing session is reopened with an explicit different model, so CLI `--session-id --model …` continuations preserve the same audit trail as interactive model switches.
- Agent tool call and collapsed result rendering now show provider/model and thinking metadata.
- Agent tool call labels inherit the parent session's live model and thinking level via a new engine `snapshot()`, so forked agent calls render the active provider/model/thinking instead of stale defaults.
- Stubbed `sessionLiveness` in the #5080 shutdown ordering regression test so its mock matches `shutdown()` now calling `this.sessionLiveness.stop()`.
- Reset the footer assistant turn count after compaction by rendering it from the same post-compaction transcript window as token/cache totals.
- Replaced a negated-OR null guard with optional chaining (`!adapter?.kill`) in `core/tools/background-tasks.ts`. Behavior-preserving.
- Surface agent-view module load failures instead of silently reporting the package as not installed.

### Changed

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: claude-bridge
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: claude-bridge
    app.kubernetes.io/component: proxy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: claude-bridge
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: claude-bridge
        app.kubernetes.io/component: proxy
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: claude-bridge

      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: ghcr-pull
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/hostname: lue-and-naddy-kube
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1000
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: claude-bridge
          image: ghcr.io/valkyriweb/claude-bridge:2026.05.31.fd487ab@sha256:99605c1f1c08c8ea32b9868d745089d2808c1db4f19b337c76de4672db8004b6
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: claude-bridge-auth
          env:
            # Bind 0.0.0.0 so the Service can reach it cross-pod.
            - name: HOST
              value: "0.0.0.0"
            - name: PORT
              value: "9100"
            - name: BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL
              value: "1h"
            - name: DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT
              value: production
            # Disable bridge-side Paperclip cost-events; Paperclip heartbeat is

            - name: PAPERCLIP_AGENT_TOKEN

            - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT

            - name: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
              value: claude-bridge
            - name: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES
              value: service.namespace=claude-bridge,deployment.environment=production,k8s.namespace.name=claude-bridge,k8s.cluster.name=lue-kube
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 9100
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: http
            failureThreshold: 10
            periodSeconds: 2
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 30
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
            runAsGroup: 1000
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]

# k8s

Parent skill. Pick the matching child reference; do not load all of them.

## Route by task

| You're about to… | Load |
|---|---|
| Query state, exec into a pod, tail logs, rollout-restart, scale, port-forward, patch a ConfigMap/Secret | `references/kubectl.md` |
| Inspect / diff / upgrade / rollback a Helm release; render a chart locally | `references/helm.md` |
| Triage a misbehaving workload — CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, pending, failing probes, weird DNS, slow node | `references/diagnostics.md` |
| Audit manifests or live workloads for security gaps (RBAC, NetworkPolicies, securityContext, Secrets, image policy) | `references/security-audit.md` |

Load with:

```ts
skill_search({ action: "get", parent: "k8s", child: "kubectl" })
```

## Tooling references

- Quick tool commands: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/TOOLS.md` → `kubectl / Kubernetes ☸️`.
- Deep tool refs: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/TOOLS/kubie.md`, `TOOLS/k9s.md`, `TOOLS/stern.md`.
- Wrappers live in `~/bin/` (on PATH in every shell, including non-interactive bash used by agents): `kube`, `kube-exec`, `kube-shell`, `kube-logs`. Prefer these over repeated long `kubectl --context ... --namespace ...` commands.

  ```
  kube lue-kube openclaw -- get pods                  # any kubectl verb after `--`
  kube lue-kube openclaw -- exec openclaw-0 -c gateway -- ls /home/node/.openclaw
  kube lue-kube openclaw -- cp -c gateway /tmp/x.md openclaw-0:/home/node/.openclaw/x.md
  kube-exec  lue-kube openclaw openclaw-0 gateway -- sh -c 'cat /etc/hostname'
  kube-shell lue-kube openclaw openclaw-0 gateway          # interactive shell
  kube-logs  lue-kube openclaw openclaw-0 gateway --tail=200
  ```

## Operating context (always-true defaults)

- **Two clusters.** `lue-kube` (personal/homelab) and `bermont-kube` (work/clients). Configs in `~/Projects/infra/{lue,bermont}-kube/`. Use `kube <context> [namespace] -- <kubectl args...>` for one-shots or `kube <context> [namespace]` for an isolated `kubie` shell; avoid mutating global context.
- **Flux is the source of truth.** Live state should match `k3s/` in the cluster repo. Drift = either someone hand-applied (bad) or Flux is paused (check `flux get kustomizations`). Don't edit live Deployments long-term — change the manifest, push, let Flux reconcile.
- **DevOps Agent RBAC** (the kubeconfigs Riley/operators use) grants cluster-wide read + mutate (no delete). Restart pattern: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/X`, never `kubectl delete pod`. See `k3s/components/devops-agent-rbac/README.md` in either repo.
- **Verify before mutating.** Read live state, dry-run with `--dry-run=server -o yaml`, then apply. For Helm: `helm diff upgrade` before `helm upgrade`.
- **No deletes.** RBAC blocks them; design around it. Need a clean slate? Force a rollout, scale to 0 then back, or recreate via manifest patch + apply.

## Cross-child notes

- `kubectl` is foundational; the other three lean on it. If unsure, start with `kubectl`.
- `diagnostics` and `security-audit` are read-mostly; both produce reports/recommendations rather than mutating directly. Hand fixes back through `kubectl` or a manifest PR.
- `helm` is reserved for chart-managed releases; raw kustomize work belongs in `kubectl`.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/k8s

# k8s

Parent skill. Pick the matching child reference; do not load all of them.

## Route by task

| You're about to… | Load |
|---|---|
| Query state, exec into a pod, tail logs, rollout-restart, scale, port-forward, patch a ConfigMap/Secret | `references/kubectl.md` |
| Inspect / diff / upgrade / rollback a Helm release; render a chart locally | `references/helm.md` |
| Triage a misbehaving workload — CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, pending, failing probes, weird DNS, slow node | `references/diagnostics.md` |
| Audit manifests or live workloads for security gaps (RBAC, NetworkPolicies, securityContext, Secrets, image policy) | `references/security-audit.md` |

Load with:

```ts
skill_search({ action: "get", parent: "k8s", child: "kubectl" })
```

## Tooling references

- Quick tool commands: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/TOOLS.md` → `kubectl / Kubernetes ☸️`.
- Deep tool refs: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/TOOLS/kubie.md`, `TOOLS/k9s.md`, `TOOLS/stern.md`.
- Wrappers live in `~/bin/` (on PATH in every shell, including non-interactive bash used by agents): `kube`, `kube-exec`, `kube-shell`, `kube-logs`. Prefer these over repeated long `kubectl --context ... --namespace ...` commands.

  ```
  kube lue-kube openclaw -- get pods                  # any kubectl verb after `--`
  kube lue-kube openclaw -- exec openclaw-0 -c gateway -- ls /home/node/.openclaw
  kube lue-kube openclaw -- cp -c gateway /tmp/x.md openclaw-0:/home/node/.openclaw/x.md
  kube-exec  lue-kube openclaw openclaw-0 gateway -- sh -c 'cat /etc/hostname'
  kube-shell lue-kube openclaw openclaw-0 gateway          # interactive shell
  kube-logs  lue-kube openclaw openclaw-0 gateway --tail=200
  ```

## Operating context (always-true defaults)

- **Two clusters.** `lue-kube` (personal/homelab) and `bermont-kube` (work/clients). Configs in `~/Projects/infra/{lue,bermont}-kube/`. Use `kube <context> [namespace] -- <kubectl args...>` for one-shots or `kube <context> [namespace]` for an isolated `kubie` shell; avoid mutating global context.
- **Flux is the source of truth.** Live state should match `k3s/` in the cluster repo. Drift = either someone hand-applied (bad) or Flux is paused (check `flux get kustomizations`). Don't edit live Deployments long-term — change the manifest, push, let Flux reconcile.
- **DevOps Agent RBAC** (the kubeconfigs Riley/operators use) grants cluster-wide read + mutate (no delete). Restart pattern: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/X`, never `kubectl delete pod`. See `k3s/components/devops-agent-rbac/README.md` in either repo.
- **Verify before mutating.** Read live state, dry-run with `--dry-run=server -o yaml`, then apply. For Helm: `helm diff upgrade` before `helm upgrade`.
- **No deletes.** RBAC blocks them; design around it. Need a clean slate? Force a rollout, scale to 0 then back, or recreate via manifest patch + apply.

## Cross-child notes

- `kubectl` is foundational; the other three lean on it. If unsure, start with `kubectl`.
- `diagnostics` and `security-audit` are read-mostly; both produce reports/recommendations rather than mutating directly. Hand fixes back through `kubectl` or a manifest PR.
- `helm` is reserved for chart-managed releases; raw kustomize work belongs in `kubectl`.

1	# Fork Changelog
2	
3	Fork-specific changes maintained by valkyriweb. Upstream package changelogs stay reserved for upstream release notes and upstreamable changes.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Changed
8	
9	- Clarified the exact-semver regex intent with a comment in `scripts/check-pinned-deps.mjs` (canary for the ported agentic-review pipeline). No behavior change.
10	- Repo chrome split from the concurrent-session checkpoint: PR template, `.gitignore` entry for nested `.pi-ws-*` worktrees, AGENTS.md guidance refresh, biome config tweak, and three `docs/goals/` session logs.
11	
12	### Fixed
13	
14	- **`setActiveToolsByName` cache-burst no-op guard (cache law #4).** Before rewriting `agent.state.tools` and rebuilding the system prompt, the method now early-returns when the freshly built `tools[]` is element-for-element **reference-identical** to the current state. An unconditional refresh on every `tools_changed`/`_refreshToolRegistry` event bursts the within-session `tools[]` (and system-prompt) cache prefix even when nothing actually changed. Reference-equality (not name-set equality) is the correct test: pi rebuilds the registry with fresh object refs whenever a definition changes (a tool gains `deferLoading`, an allowlist empties), so a genuine change yields different refs and the rebuild proceeds — only a true no-op early-returns (mirrors pi-ai's `convertedToolCache` WeakMap keyed by tool reference). Guard is skipped until the base prompt has been built once (`_baseSystemPromptOptions` is set only by `_rebuildSystemPrompt`), so the cold init `empty→empty` rebuild still runs. Same change adds the post-registration **deferral-override seam** (`setDeferredToolOverrides`/`_applyDeferredOverrides`): extensions can force already-registered tools to `deferLoading:true` so they ride `tools[]` as `defer_loading` stubs across every registry rebuild, with the same unchanged-set no-op guard (`sameStringSet`) so a redundant call doesn't burst the prefix. Also threads the live agent state into `createPromptCacheAffinityKey` on every model switch so the affinity key tracks the actual model rather than a stale cwd-only key.
15	- **Changelog guard: package-level test-only changes no longer wrongly require a CHANGELOG.** `requiredChangelog()` in `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` returned the package `CHANGELOG.md` for any `packages/<pkg>/` path before consulting `isIgnored()` (which already covers test-only paths via `isTestOnly()`), so a change touching only `packages/<pkg>/test/**` failed the guard, contradicting the script's own "tests-only ... are ignored" message and the AGENTS changelog rules. Now `isIgnored(path)` is checked first (returns no requirement), then package/fork resolution. Verified with crafted diffs: a package test-only change passes, a package src change without its CHANGELOG still fails.
16	- **Workflow shellcheck hygiene: quoted `$(which fdfind)` and grouped `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` redirects so `actionlint` (incl. shellcheck) is clean.** SC2046 (word-splitting on unquoted command substitution) in `ci.yml`, `build-binaries.yml`, and `release.yml`; SC2129 (consecutive redirects) in the `upstream-sync.yml` conflict branch. Behavior-preserving; lets the new `workflow-sanity.yml` gate pass on day one.
17	- **`fork-safety-check` CI: reordered `npm run build` so the four workspace packages build before `test:build-gate` runs.** The root `build` script ran `test:build-gate` first, but the gate's `test:e2e` step (`packages/coding-agent` `test/suite`) imports `@valkyriweb/pi-tui/dist/index.js` via `modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts`. Because `packages/tui` had not been built yet, the gate crashed with `Cannot find package '.../@valkyriweb/pi-tui/dist/index.js'`, failing the `Build workspace declarations` step on every PR. New order: `tui → ai → agent → coding-agent`, then `test:build-gate` last, so the gate runs against freshly built dist (its intent — catching prompt-cache/system-prompt regressions before a build ships — is unchanged). Also guarded the gate's `test:my-pi-extensions` step (`npm --prefix ../my-pi run test:extension-gate:ci`) to skip when the `my-pi` sibling repo is absent: on CI the sibling is not checked out, so the step now fails with `ENOENT .../my-pi/package.json` once the earlier crash is gone. The guard runs the extension gate locally (where `../my-pi` exists) and skips with a notice on CI. Finally, gave the `fork-safety-check` Checkout `fetch-depth: 0` so the job's `npm run check` step (`check:changelog` runs `git diff origin/main...HEAD`) can resolve `origin/main` on CI — the previous shallow checkout made that diff fail with `unknown revision origin/main` once the build step stopped crashing first (mirrors the standalone `changelog.yml` workflow, which already uses `fetch-depth: 0`).
18	
19	### Changed
20	
21	- Synced `upstream/main` (incl. OpenAI GPT-5.5 thinking-metadata fix). Resolved merge conflicts in `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (kept the fork's `convertMessages(..., supportsDeferredTools, allowEmptySignature)` superset call and the no-`cache_control`-on-tools rationale) and `packages/ai/CHANGELOG.md` (unioned both release notes); regenerated `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` to dedupe the concatenated model blocks while preserving the fork's cloudflare-gateway models. Also ignored `.pi/workflows/` run artifacts.
22	- **Bash foreground-timeout moved behind an additive `onBashTimeout` seam; core default is now upstream-neutral (kill).** The exec loop no longer hardcodes a detach policy; on timeout it consults a pluggable resolver given a `BashTimeout` context (`command`, `cwd`, `timeoutMs`, `background()`, `kill()`) and acts on the `BashTimeoutOutcome` (`{ backgroundedJobId }` or `{ failed }`). The **core default kills and reports `Command timed out after Ns`** (closest to upstream); the opinionated detach-on-timeout policy lives in the my-pi `native-tool-aliases` extension, which calls the exported `onBashTimeout((t) => ({ backgroundedJobId: t.background().id }))` so Luke's `Bash` tool auto-backgrounds (Claude Code parity) while core stays neutral. Consumers override via `onBashTimeout(resolver)` (returns a restore fn) to detach, kill, log, or gate — without reshaping the upstream exec path (one call deep). Honours the additive-hooks principle: `core/tools/bash.ts` keeps its shape, the policy lives in the extension. Exported `onBashTimeout` + `BashTimeout`/`BashTimeoutOutcome` types from the package barrel. Seamed e2e coverage in `test/bash-timeout-background.test.ts`: default kill+timeout report, override-to-detach + bg read, and override-to-fail (seam sees real command/timeout, restore returns to default).
23	- **Fork-mode sub-agent prefix: switched from strip to placeholder-substitute (CC parity).** `getFilteredForkMessages` in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/agents/context.ts` used to drop parent `agent`/`subagent` `tool_use` blocks (and any associated `tool_result`s) from the fork child's message history. That broke prompt-cache continuity: the moment a stripped tool_use appeared in parent's actual cached prefix, every subsequent block in the child's request diverged byte-for-byte from the parent's cache key, busting cache reuse for the entire leading section. New behavior mirrors Claude Code 2.1.x `buildForkedMessages` (`src/tools/AgentTool/forkSubagent.ts`): keep parent's `tool_use` blocks in place, and for any unresolved `tool_use` (denied or simply incomplete at fork time) synthesize a fixed-bytes placeholder `tool_result` with text `"Sibling agent task in progress."`. New helper `substitutePlaceholdersForUnresolvedToolCalls` is exported alongside `getFilteredForkMessages`. The placeholder text is identical across every fork child spawned from the same parent state, so **sibling forks share cache with each other**, not just with the parent — the critical property for wide parallel fan-out via `tasks[]`. Cache parity contract: any two `getFilteredForkMessages(parentSession)` calls return byte-identical arrays through every leading block, with the per-child user directive (built by `buildChildTaskPrompt`) as the only divergence point. Removed the now-dead `filterDeniedToolArtifacts` helper; left a comment marker so future maintainers see the historical rationale. Regression tests in `packages/coding-agent/test/agent-context-inheritance.test.ts`: "fork filtering keeps parent agent/subagent tool_uses for cache parity", "fork filtering substitutes placeholders for unresolved tool_uses, drops orphan results", and "sibling forks produce byte-identical message arrays" (JSON.stringify equality on two consecutive `getFilteredForkMessages` calls). Side note: orphan `tool_result`s (results whose `tool_use` doesn't exist in the message stream) are still dropped — those would confuse the provider API and don't appear in parent's cached prefix anyway.
24	
25	### Added
26	
27	- **Session liveness markers + resume-picker "open elsewhere" badge.** Each interactive pi process now advertises which session file it has open by writing a `<sessionPath>.live` sidecar (`{pid, startedAt, heartbeat}`) next to the session `.jsonl`, refreshed on a 5s `unref`'d timer and removed on shutdown (`init`/`shutdown`/`emergencyTerminalExit` in `modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts`; marker moves to the resumed session in `handleResumeSession`). New core module `core/session-liveness.ts` exposes `SessionLiveness` (writer) and `listActiveSessionPaths` (reader): a marker counts as live only when its owning pid is alive (`process.kill(pid, 0)`, treating `EPERM` as alive) **and** its heartbeat is fresher than 20s; stale/dead markers are reaped on read. The resume picker (`modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts`, used by both `/resume` and the `--resume` startup picker in `cli/session-picker.ts`) badges such sessions with a green `●` and `success` color, never flagging its own current session. Liveness is per-process runtime state in session-dir sidecars — it never enters the cached system prompt or `tools[]`. Regression: `test/session-liveness.test.ts` (8 cases). Logged in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` as `fork-first (platform)`.
28	- **Project-SDLC governance set (full).** Added `VISION.md` (fork purpose, non-goals, release posture), `SECURITY.md` (private vulnerability reporting + upstream pointer), `docs/RELEASING.md` (canonical release runbook mirroring the AGENTS.md "Releasing" section, which now points to it), `.github/CODEOWNERS` (`@valkyriweb`; release/security-sensitive paths called out), `.github/dependabot.yml` (weekly grouped github-actions + npm minor/patch, capped open-PRs; `pr-gate.yml` already skips `dependabot[bot]`), `.github/labeler.yml` + `.github/workflows/labeler.yml` (path → label routing; the `pkg:*` labels must be created in the fork first — see the labeler.yml header for `gh label create` commands), and `.github/workflows/workflow-sanity.yml` (actionlint via pinned `docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12`, triggered on `.github/workflows/**`). Closes the project-sdlc audit gaps that fit a personal fork; per-package CHANGELOGs + this FORK-CHANGELOG remain the release-notes source of truth (the audit's root-`CHANGELOG.md` "gap" is a false positive).
29	- **`@valkyriweb/pi-*` fork package scope and GitHub Packages publish seam.** The four publishable fork packages (`pi-ai`, `pi-agent-core`, `pi-tui`, `pi-coding-agent`) now use lockstep `0.78.0-luke.0` versions under the `@valkyriweb` scope, with GitHub Packages `publishConfig` and `.npmrc` scope routing. Internal dependencies, TS path aliases, package-manager smoke scripts, shrinkwrap generation, README/test imports, and local/publish release scripts were moved to the new scope so emitted JS does not reference upstream `@earendil-works/*` packages.
30	- **`maxTurns` hard turn cap for the agent loop, surfaced through `ctx.forkAgent({ maxTurns })`** (mirrors Claude Code's `query({ maxTurns })`). A new first-class field on `AgentLoopConfig` (`packages/agent/src/types.ts`) and the `Agent` engine (`AgentOptions.maxTurns` + public `Agent.maxTurns`, threaded into `createLoopConfig`). `runLoop` (`packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts`) counts completed assistant turns and, when the count reaches `maxTurns`, emits `agent_end` and returns **before** starting another LLM call — even if the model still wants to call tools — giving a deterministic safety bound for runaway agentic forks (e.g. background memory extractors). Plumbed into coding-agent via `AgentTaskConfig.maxTurns` (`core/agents/types.ts`), set on the child engine in `runChild` (`core/agents/executor.ts`) before driving, exposed on `ForkAgentOptions.maxTurns` (`core/extensions/types.ts`), and mapped through `engine.fork` (`core/agents/engine.ts`). Undefined or `<= 0` = unbounded; the built-in `agent` tool schema is intentionally left unchanged (cache-stable `tools[]`). Regression: `packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts` "should stop after maxTurns assistant turns even if the model keeps calling tools" (a stream that always returns a tool call halts at exactly `maxTurns`).
31	- **`ToolDefinition.replacesBuiltins` — extensions can drop core base builtins they supersede.** An extension-registered override declares the lowercase base builtins it fully replaces (e.g. my-pi `native-tool-overrides`' `Read`/`Edit`/… declare `["read"]`/`["edit"]`/… and `TaskOutput`/`TaskStop` declare `["bash_output"]`/`["bash_kill"]`). `AgentSession._refreshToolRegistry` collects the declarations from the live extension tool set and drops the named builtins from both `_toolDefinitions` (so `getAllTools()` omits them) and `_toolRegistry` (so they can't be activated), so a consumer that force-activates the whole registry (e.g. rusty-wa) no longer surfaces duplicate `Read`/`read` schemas. No declaration ⇒ base tools stay, so vanilla/upstream sessions are unaffected. Resolved once at registry build (no per-turn state) so the `tools[]` prefix stays cache-stable. Optional field on `ToolDefinition` (`core/extensions/types.ts`) + filter in `core/agent-session.ts`. Regression: `test/suite/regressions/replaces-builtins.test.ts` (drops when declared, keeps when not); fork `test:build-gate` green.
32	- **Auto-background-on-timeout for the built-in `bash` tool** (mirrors Claude Code's `tengu_bash_command_timeout_backgrounded`). Instead of killing a timed-out foreground command, the exec layer now **detaches the still-running process** and adopts it into the background-job registry (`adoptBashBackground` in `core/tools/bash.ts`): a race between real exit and the timeout resolves to `{ exitCode: null, backgroundedJobId }`, the foreground `onData` listeners are detached, future stdout/stderr is redirected to `~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log`, and the adopted child's pid stays tracked (the bg job owns it). The result reports the `bgId`/`pid` and that the process was **not** killed. Read live output with `bash_output(bgId)`, stop with `bash_kill(bgId)`. The `timeout` param description documents the behavior. (Custom `BashOperations` that still throw the legacy `timeout:` sentinel fall back to a plain timeout error.)
33	- Added a root `test:build-gate` script run by `npm run build` after the four workspace packages are built. The gate runs the fork's system-prompt boundary tests, cache-stable tool/defer-loading tests, coding-agent suite integration tests, and the sibling `my-pi` extension/profile cache contract so prompt-cache regressions fail before a new local build ships.
34	- Added a PR changelog guard (`scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` plus `.github/workflows/changelog.yml`) and wired it into `npm run check` so package code changes must update the matching package `CHANGELOG.md`, while root/scripts changes must update `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`.
35	- Added **`"child-agent"` to `InputSource`** and threaded source through `BeforeAgentStartEvent.source`, `ExtensionContext.source`, `AgentSessionConfig.source`, `CreateAgentSessionOptions.source`, `CreateAgentSessionFromServicesOptions.source`, and a new `pi --source <interactive|rpc|extension|child-agent>` CLI flag (`packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts`). Built-in `agent` tool / `ctx.forkAgent` now tag every in-process delegated AgentSession with `source: "child-agent"` AND pass `source: "child-agent"` per-prompt; out-of-process Pi children spawned by extensions (e.g. dream-memory's agentic dream) pass `--source child-agent` on the CLI. Replaces the legacy `PI_MEMORY_SUBAGENT=1` env contract that dream-memory / pi-memory used to detect sub-agent runs — the env var was a race waiting to happen under parallel `forkAgent` fan-out sharing one Node process. Now memory extensions read `event.source` (per-turn, handles extension steers) or `ctx.source` (session-level, handles `turn_end` / `session_shutdown` / `tool_call` / `tool_result` / `memory_note` tool execution where no event-level source exists). Per-turn `triggerTurn`-driven calls (e.g. pi-goal's `pendingControlPrompt`) emit `before_agent_start` with `source: "extension"` so memory hooks skip the synthetic turn too. Regression tests: `before-agent-start-source.test.ts` (per-turn source plumbing + agent tool tags `"child-agent"`), `args.test.ts` (CLI flag + valid-value enforcement + diagnostic on invalid), `print-mode.test.ts` (forwards source to `session.prompt`). Also fixed `params.tasks?.map is not a function` on the agent tool: added `coerceTaskList()` in `core/tools/agent.ts` that handles JSON-stringified tasks/chain and single-object inputs from providers whose schema validation is lax; covered by `agent-tool-tasks-coercion.test.ts`.
36	- Added a per-agent **bash policy** scaffold in the built-in `bash` tool, enforced via `AsyncLocalStorage` so no plumbing through session factories. New exports from `core/tools/bash.ts`: `BashPolicy` (`label`, `denyCommands`, `denyWrites`), `runWithBashPolicy(policy, fn)`, `checkBashPolicy(command, policy)`, and `EXPLORE_BASH_POLICY`. The matcher tokenizes the command into pipeline/sequence segments, then runs a multi-word prefix pass (e.g. `git push`) plus a single-word any-token pass (e.g. `rm`, catches `find ... | xargs rm`); rejects unquoted `>` / `>>` / `tee` / `sponge` when `denyWrites` is set; and pre-rejects command substitution (`$(...)`, backticks), here-docs (`<<WORD`, `<<-WORD`), with single-quoted spans stripped first to avoid false positives on literal text. Soft guard, not a sandbox — documented limitations. The agents executor binds `EXPLORE_BASH_POLICY` around `session.prompt(...)` whenever the child agent id is `explore`.
37	- Enabled `bash` for the built-in `explore` agent (mirrors Claude Code's `Explore` tool surface), gated by `EXPLORE_BASH_POLICY`. Explore can now run read-only git inspection (`git status/log/diff/show/blame`), file inspection (`cat`/`head`/`tail`/`wc`/`stat`), discovery (`which`/`type`), and read-only `gh` queries (`gh pr view`/`gh issue view`/`gh api -X GET`). Mutating commands (rm/mv/cp/git push/git commit/npm install/kubectl apply/sed -i/output redirection/etc.) are rejected at the executor with a clear reason fed back to the model. Description, system prompt, and trigger phrases updated to match. The `general` agent description is tightened to push pure read-only investigation back to `explore`.
38	- Added **B5 TUI slot extension hooks** to the `ExtensionAPI`: `pi.registerMainPane(id, factory)` / `showMainPane(id, payload?)` / `hideMainPane(id)` (push a component into `chatContainer`'s content stack); `pi.registerOverlay(id, factory)` / `showOverlay(id, payload?)` / `hideOverlay(id)` (durable overlay registration, distinct from one-shot `ui.custom()`); `pi.registerFooter(id, spec)` (contribute a focusable child into the existing footer's nav chain without owning the whole footer; reactive `visible()` predicate). Spatial/slot extension points (`register*`) deliberately distinct from temporal hooks (`on*` for `session_start`/`turn_end`/etc.). Runner exposes `getRegisteredMainPane(id)`, `getRegisteredOverlay(id)`, `getRegisteredFooters()`, plus `bindSlotUI()` for UI-capable modes (interactive) to back the imperative show/hide API; non-UI modes (RPC/print) keep the default no-op stubs so show/hide calls silently swallow. Implementation lands the hook surface; the interactive-mode mount-into-`chatContainer` wiring lives in the fork-only zoom consumer (issue 12 extracts that into `pi-agent-ui`). Design [`docs/plans/b5-tui-hooks-design-proposal-2026-05-21.md`](my-pi/docs/plans/b5-tui-hooks-design-proposal-2026-05-21.md) approved by Luke 2026-05-22; 14 unit tests in `extensions-runner-b5-hooks.test.ts` cover registration, show/hide delegation, first-registration-wins, reactive footer visibility, and no-registration baseline.
39	- Added `triggerTokens` to `compaction` settings — an absolute context-token threshold for auto-compaction. When the active model's context window is known, Pi derives `reserveTokens` as `contextWindow - triggerTokens`; otherwise falls back to the configured `reserveTokens`. Not yet upstream (FORK-CHANGELOG previously claimed PR #5 — that PR is unrelated; no upstream PR exists for this change as of 2026-05-21).
40	- Added `run_in_background`, `bash_output(bgId)`, and `bash_kill(bgId)` to the built-in `bash` tool, mirroring Claude Code's `BashOutput`/`KillShell` API. Background jobs spawn detached (POSIX), append stdout/stderr to `~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log`, and the registry is reaped via `killAllBashBgJobs()` from `AgentSession.dispose()` so processes don't leak across `/clear`, fork, switchSession, reload, or final shutdown. Bounded log slices for `bash_output`, idempotent `bash_kill`, and a teardown test that confirms registry cleanup.
