Behavior-preserving; lets the new `workflow-sanity.yml` gate pass on day one.
- **`fork-safety-check` CI: reordered `npm run build` so the four workspace packages build before `test:build-gate` runs.** The root `build` script ran `test:build-gate` first, but the gate's `test:e2e` step (`packages/coding-agent` `test/suite`) imports `@valkyriweb/pi-tui/dist/index.js` via `modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts`. Because `packages/tui` had not been built yet, the gate crashed with `Cannot find package '.../@valkyriweb/pi-tui/dist/index.js'`, failing the `Build workspace declarations` step on every PR. New order: `tui → ai → agent → coding-agent`, then `test:build-gate` last, so the gate runs against freshly built dist (its intent — catching prompt-cache/system-prompt regressions before a build ships — is unchanged). Also guarded the gate's `test:my-pi-extensions` step (`npm --prefix ../my-pi run test:extension-gate:ci`) to skip when the `my-pi` sibling repo is absent: on CI the sibling is not checked out, so the step now fails with `ENOENT .../my-pi/package.json` once the earlier crash is gone. The guard runs the extension gate locally (where `../my-pi` exists) and skips with a notice on CI. Finally, gave the `fork-safety-check` Checkout `fetch-depth: 0` so the job's `npm run check` step (`check:changelog` runs `git diff origin/main...HEAD`) can resolve `origin/main` on CI — the previous shallow checkout made that diff fail with `unknown revision origin/main` once the build step stopped crashing first (mirrors the standalone `changelog.yml` workflow, which already uses `fetch-depth: 0`).

### Changed

- Synced `upstream/main` (incl. OpenAI GPT-5.5 thinking-metadata fix). Resolved merge conflicts in `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (kept the fork's `convertMessages(..., supportsDeferredTools, allowEmptySignature)` superset call and the no-`cache_control`-on-tools rationale) and `packages/ai/CHANGELOG.md` (unioned both release notes); regenerated `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` to dedupe the concatenated model blocks while preserving the fork's cloudflare-gateway models. Also ignored `.pi/workflows/` run artifacts.
- **Bash foreground-timeout moved behind an additive `onBashTimeout` seam; core default is now upstream-neutral (kill).** The exec loop no longer hardcodes a detach policy; on timeout it consults a pluggable resolver given a `BashTimeout` context (`command`, `cwd`, `timeoutMs`, `background()`, `kill()`) and acts on the `BashTimeoutOutcome` (`{ backgroundedJobId }` or `{ failed }`). The **core default kills and reports `Command timed out after Ns`** (closest to upstream); the opinionated detach-on-timeout policy lives in the my-pi `native-tool-aliases` extension, which calls the exported `onBashTimeout((t) => ({ backgroundedJobId: t.background().id }))` so Luke's `Bash` tool auto-backgrounds (Claude Code parity) while core stays neutral. Consumers override via `onBashTimeout(resolver)` (returns a restore fn) to detach, kill, log, or gate — without reshaping the upstream exec path (one call deep). Honours the additive-hooks principle: `core/tools/bash.ts` keeps its shape, the policy lives in the extension. Exported `onBashTimeout` + `BashTimeout`/`BashTimeoutOutcome` types from the package barrel. Seamed e2e coverage in `test/bash-timeout-background.test.ts`: default kill+timeout report, override-to-detach + bg read, and override-to-fail (seam sees real command/timeout, restore returns to default).
- **Fork-mode sub-agent prefix: switched from strip to placeholder-substitute (CC parity).** `getFilteredForkMessages` in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/agents/context.ts` used to drop parent `agent`/`subagent` `tool_use` blocks (and any associated `tool_result`s) from the fork child's message history. That broke prompt-cache continuity: the moment a stripped tool_use appeared in parent's actual cached prefix, every subsequent block in the child's request diverged byte-for-byte from the parent's cache key, busting cache reuse for the entire leading section. New behavior mirrors Claude Code 2.1.x `buildForkedMessages` (`src/tools/AgentTool/forkSubagent.ts`): keep parent's `tool_use` blocks in place, and for any unresolved `tool_use` (denied or simply incomplete at fork time) synthesize a fixed-bytes placeholder `tool_result` with text `"Sibling agent task in progress."`. New helper `substitutePlaceholdersForUnresolvedToolCalls` is exported alongside `getFilteredForkMessages`. The placeholder text is identical across every fork child spawned from the same parent state, so **sibling forks share cache with each other**, not just with the parent — the critical property for wide parallel fan-out via `tasks[]`. Cache parity contract: any two `getFilteredForkMessages(parentSession)` calls return byte-identical arrays through every leading block, with the per-child user directive (built by `buildChildTaskPrompt`) as the only divergence point. Removed the now-dead `filterDeniedToolArtifacts` helper; left a comment marker so future maintainers see the historical rationale. Regression tests in `packages/coding-agent/test/agent-context-inheritance.test.ts`: "fork filtering keeps parent agent/subagent tool_uses for cache parity", "fork filtering substitutes placeholders for unresolved tool_uses, drops orphan results", and "sibling forks produce byte-identical message arrays" (JSON.stringify equality on two consecutive `getFilteredForkMessages` calls). Side note: orphan `tool_result`s (results whose `tool_use` doesn't exist in the message stream) are still dropped — those would confuse the provider API and don't appear in parent's cached prefix anyway.

### Added

- **Session liveness markers + resume-picker "open elsewhere" badge.** Each interactive pi process now advertises which session file it has open by writing a `<sessionPath>.live` sidecar (`{pid, startedAt, heartbeat}`) next to the session `.jsonl`, refreshed on a 5s `unref`'d timer and removed on shutdown (`init`/`shutdown`/`emergencyTerminalExit` in `modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts`; marker moves to the resumed session in `handleResumeSession`). New core module `core/session-liveness.ts` exposes `SessionLiveness` (writer) and `listActiveSessionPaths` (reader): a marker counts as live only when its owning pid is alive (`process.kill(pid, 0)`, treating `EPERM` as alive) **and** its heartbeat is fresher than 20s; stale/dead markers are reaped on read. The resume picker (`modes/interactive/components/session-selector.ts`, used by both `/resume` and the `--resume` startup picker in `cli/session-picker.ts`) badges such sessions with a green `●` and `success` color, never flagging its own current session. Liveness is per-process runtime state in session-dir sidecars — it never enters the cached system prompt or `tools[]`. Regression: `test/session-liveness.test.ts` (8 cases). Logged in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` as `fork-first (platform)`.
- **Project-SDLC governance set (full).** Added `VISION.md` (fork purpose, non-goals, release posture), `SECURITY.md` (private vulnerability reporting + upstream pointer), `docs/RELEASING.md` (canonical release runbook mirroring the AGENTS.md "Releasing" section, which now points to it), `.github/CODEOWNERS` (`@valkyriweb`; release/security-sensitive paths called out), `.github/dependabot.yml` (weekly grouped github-actions + npm minor/patch, capped open-PRs; `pr-gate.yml` already skips `dependabot[bot]`), `.github/labeler.yml` + `.github/workflows/labeler.yml` (path → label routing; the `pkg:*` labels must be created in the fork first — see the labeler.yml header for `gh label create` commands), and `.github/workflows/workflow-sanity.yml` (actionlint via pinned `docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12`, triggered on `.github/workflows/**`). Closes the project-sdlc audit gaps that fit a personal fork; per-package CHANGELOGs + this FORK-CHANGELOG remain the release-notes source of truth (the audit's root-`CHANGELOG.md` "gap" is a false positive).
- **`@valkyriweb/pi-*` fork package scope and GitHub Packages publish seam.** The four publishable fork packages (`pi-ai`, `pi-agent-core`, `pi-tui`, `pi-coding-agent`) now use lockstep `0.78.0-luke.0` versions under the `@valkyriweb` scope, with GitHub Packages `publishConfig` and `.npmrc` scope routing. Internal dependencies, TS path aliases, package-manager smoke scripts, shrinkwrap generation, README/test imports, and local/publish release scripts were moved to the new scope so emitted JS does not reference upstream `@earendil-works/*` packages.
- **`maxTurns` hard turn cap for the agent loop, surfaced through `ctx.forkAgent({ maxTurns })`** (mirrors Claude Code's `query({ maxTurns })`). A new first-class field on `AgentLoopConfig` (`packages/agent/src/types.ts`) and the `Agent` engine (`AgentOptions.maxTurns` + public `Agent.maxTurns`, threaded into `createLoopConfig`). `runLoop` (`packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts`) counts completed assistant turns and, when the count reaches `maxTurns`, emits `agent_end` and returns **before** starting another LLM call — even if the model still wants to call tools — giving a deterministic safety bound for runaway agentic forks (e.g. background memory extractors). Plumbed into coding-agent via `AgentTaskConfig.maxTurns` (`core/agents/types.ts`), set on the child engine in `runChild` (`core/agents/executor.ts`) before driving, exposed on `ForkAgentOptions.maxTurns` (`core/extensions/types.ts`), and mapped through `engine.fork` (`core/agents/engine.ts`). Undefined or `<= 0` = unbounded; the built-in `agent` tool schema is intentionally left unchanged (cache-stable `tools[]`). Regression: `packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts` "should stop after maxTurns assistant turns even if the model keeps calling tools" (a stream that always returns a tool call halts at exactly `maxTurns`).
- **`ToolDefinition.replacesBuiltins` — extensions can drop core base builtins they supersede.** An extension-registered override declares the lowercase base builtins it fully replaces (e.g. my-pi `native-tool-overrides`' `Read`/`Edit`/… declare `["read"]`/`["edit"]`/… and `TaskOutput`/`TaskStop` declare `["bash_output"]`/`["bash_kill"]`). `AgentSession._refreshToolRegistry` collects the declarations from the live extension tool set and drops the named builtins from both `_toolDefinitions` (so `getAllTools()` omits them) and `_toolRegistry` (so they can't be activated), so a consumer that force-activates the whole registry (e.g. rusty-wa) no longer surfaces duplicate `Read`/`read` schemas. No declaration ⇒ base tools stay, so vanilla/upstream sessions are unaffected. Resolved once at registry build (no per-turn state) so the `tools[]` prefix stays cache-stable. Optional field on `ToolDefinition` (`core/extensions/types.ts`) + filter in `core/agent-session.ts`. Regression: `test/suite/regressions/replaces-builtins.test.ts` (drops when declared, keeps when not); fork `test:build-gate` green.
- **Auto-background-on-timeout for the built-in `bash` tool** (mirrors Claude Code's `tengu_bash_command_timeout_backgrounded`). Instead of killing a timed-out foreground command, the exec layer now **detaches the still-running process** and adopts it into the background-job registry (`adoptBashBackground` in `core/tools/bash.ts`): a race between real exit and the timeout resolves to `{ exitCode: null, backgroundedJobId }`, the foreground `onData` listeners are detached, future stdout/stderr is redirected to `~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log`, and the adopted child's pid stays tracked (the bg job owns it). The result reports the `bgId`/`pid` and that the process was **not** killed. Read live output with `bash_output(bgId)`, stop with `bash_kill(bgId)`. The `timeout` param description documents the behavior. (Custom `BashOperations` that still throw the legacy `timeout:` sentinel fall back to a plain timeout error.)
- Added a root `test:build-gate` script run by `npm run build` after the four workspace packages are built. The gate runs the fork's system-prompt boundary tests, cache-stable tool/defer-loading tests, coding-agent suite integration tests, and the sibling `my-pi` extension/profile cache contract so prompt-cache regressions fail before a new local build ships.
- Added a PR changelog guard (`scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` plus `.github/workflows/changelog.yml`) and wired it into `npm run check` so package code changes must update the matching package `CHANGELOG.md`, while root/scripts changes must update `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`.
- Added **`"child-agent"` to `InputSource`** and threaded source through `BeforeAgentStartEvent.source`, `ExtensionContext.source`, `AgentSessionConfig.source`, `CreateAgentSessionOptions.source`, `CreateAgentSessionFromServicesOptions.source`, and a new `pi --source <interactive|rpc|extension|child-agent>` CLI flag (`packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts`). Built-in `agent` tool / `ctx.forkAgent` now tag every in-process delegated AgentSession with `source: "child-agent"` AND pass `source: "child-agent"` per-prompt; out-of-process Pi children spawned by extensions (e.g. dream-memory's agentic dream) pass `--source child-agent` on the CLI. Replaces the legacy `PI_MEMORY_SUBAGENT=1` env contract that dream-memory / pi-memory used to detect sub-agent runs — the env var was a race waiting to happen under parallel `forkAgent` fan-out sharing one Node process. Now memory extensions read `event.source` (per-turn, handles extension steers) or `ctx.source` (session-level, handles `turn_end` / `session_shutdown` / `tool_call` / `tool_result` / `memory_note` tool execution where no event-level source exists). Per-turn `triggerTurn`-driven calls (e.g. pi-goal's `pendingControlPrompt`) emit `before_agent_start` with `source: "extension"` so memory hooks skip the synthetic turn too. Regression tests: `before-agent-start-source.test.ts` (per-turn source plumbing + agent tool tags `"child-agent"`), `args.test.ts` (CLI flag + valid-value enforcement + diagnostic on invalid), `print-mode.test.ts` (forwards source to `session.prompt`). Also fixed `params.tasks?.map is not a function` on the agent tool: added `coerceTaskList()` in `core/tools/agent.ts` that handles JSON-stringified tasks/chain and single-object inputs from providers whose schema validation is lax; covered by `agent-tool-tasks-coercion.test.ts`.
- Added a per-agent **bash policy** scaffold in the built-in `bash` tool, enforced via `AsyncLocalStorage` so no plumbing through session factories. New exports from `core/tools/bash.ts`: `BashPolicy` (`label`, `denyCommands`, `denyWrites`), `runWithBashPolicy(policy, fn)`, `checkBashPolicy(command, policy)`, and `EXPLORE_BASH_POLICY`. The matcher tokenizes the command into pipeline/sequence segments, then runs a multi-word prefix pass (e.g. `git push`) plus a single-word any-token pass (e.g. `rm`, catches `find ... | xargs rm`); rejects unquoted `>` / `>>` / `tee` / `sponge` when `denyWrites` is set; and pre-rejects command substitution (`$(...)`, backticks), here-docs (`<<WORD`, `<<-WORD`), with single-quoted spans stripped first to avoid false positives on literal text. Soft guard, not a sandbox — documented limitations. The agents executor binds `EXPLORE_BASH_POLICY` around `session.prompt(...)` whenever the child agent id is `explore`.
- Enabled `bash` for the built-in `explore` agent (mirrors Claude Code's `Explore` tool surface), gated by `EXPLORE_BASH_POLICY`. Explore can now run read-only git inspection (`git status/log/diff/show/blame`), file inspection (`cat`/`head`/`tail`/`wc`/`stat`), discovery (`which`/`type`), and read-only `gh` queries (`gh pr view`/`gh issue view`/`gh api -X GET`). Mutating commands (rm/mv/cp/git push/git commit/npm install/kubectl apply/sed -i/output redirection/etc.) are rejected at the executor with a clear reason fed back to the model. Description, system prompt, and trigger phrases updated to match. The `general` agent description is tightened to push pure read-only investigation back to `explore`.
- Added **B5 TUI slot extension hooks** to the `ExtensionAPI`: `pi.registerMainPane(id, factory)` / `showMainPane(id, payload?)` / `hideMainPane(id)` (push a component into `chatContainer`'s content stack); `pi.registerOverlay(id, factory)` / `showOverlay(id, payload?)` / `hideOverlay(id)` (durable overlay registration, distinct from one-shot `ui.custom()`); `pi.registerFooter(id, spec)` (contribute a focusable child into the existing footer's nav chain without owning the whole footer; reactive `visible()` predicate). Spatial/slot extension points (`register*`) deliberately distinct from temporal hooks (`on*` for `session_start`/`turn_end`/etc.). Runner exposes `getRegisteredMainPane(id)`, `getRegisteredOverlay(id)`, `getRegisteredFooters()`, plus `bindSlotUI()` for UI-capable modes (interactive) to back the imperative show/hide API; non-UI modes (RPC/print) keep the default no-op stubs so show/hide calls silently swallow. Implementation lands the hook surface; the interactive-mode mount-into-`chatContainer` wiring lives in the fork-only zoom consumer (issue 12 extracts that into `pi-agent-ui`). Design [`docs/plans/b5-tui-hooks-design-proposal-2026-05-21.md`](my-pi/docs/plans/b5-tui-hooks-design-proposal-2026-05-21.md) approved by Luke 2026-05-22; 14 unit tests in `extensions-runner-b5-hooks.test.ts` cover registration, show/hide delegation, first-registration-wins, reactive footer visibility, and no-registration baseline.
- Added `triggerTokens` to `compaction` settings — an absolute context-token threshold for auto-compaction. When the active model's context window is known, Pi derives `reserveTokens` as `contextWindow - triggerTokens`; otherwise falls back to the configured `reserveTokens`. Not yet upstream (FORK-CHANGELOG previously claimed PR #5 — that PR is unrelated; no upstream PR exists for this change as of 2026-05-21).
- Added `run_in_background`, `bash_output(bgId)`, and `bash_kill(bgId)` to the built-in `bash` tool, mirroring Claude Code's `BashOutput`/`KillShell` API. Background jobs spawn detached (POSIX), append stdout/stderr to `~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log`, and the registry is reaped via `killAllBashBgJobs()` from `AgentSession.dispose()` so processes don't leak across `/clear`, fork, switchSession, reload, or final shutdown. Bounded log slices for `bash_output`, idempotent `bash_kill`, and a teardown test that confirms registry cleanup.

name: Release

# Automated Changesets release loop (industry-standard pattern).
#
# Changesets belongs here, in checked-in release automation — not as the official
# GitHub App PR nag bot. PR-time missing-changeset classification is handled by
# repo-local CI/ClawSweeper guards; this workflow owns version + publish.
#
# Runs on every push to main, but only ACTS when there is release work:
#  - pending changesets on main  -> opens/updates the "Version Packages" PR
#    (runs `version`, bumps versions + CHANGELOGs). No publish.
#  - the commit that MERGES that PR (changesets consumed, versions bumped,
#    packages not yet on the registry) -> runs `publish` + pushes tags.
#  - nothing to release -> no-op.
#
# Stability gate: PRs opened by the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN do NOT trigger other
# workflows (GitHub recursion guard), so ci.yml never runs on the workflow's
# Version Packages PR. To keep the cache/prompt-stability gate blocking before publish,
# this job runs `gate:ci` (the same portable checks ci.yml runs, shared via the
# npm script) as a step BEFORE changesets/action — a red gate fails the job and
# publish never runs.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:   # manual re-trigger (e.g. after merging the Version PR)

# Never run two release jobs at once (avoids racing Version PR updates / double publish).
concurrency: release-${{ github.ref }}

permissions:
  contents: write        # create/update the Version PR commit + push tags
  pull-requests: write   # open/update the Version Packages PR
  packages: write        # publish to GitHub Packages (@valkyriweb scope)

env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0   # changesets needs full history + tags

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      # Nested pnpm-lock.yaml files (dream-memory, letta/mem0-shadow, oracle) make
      # Changesets resolve pnpm as the publish tool — install it like ci.yml does.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - run: npm ci

      # Blocking stability gate — must pass before any publish (see header note).
      - run: npm run gate:ci

      - name: Create Release PR or publish
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          version: npm run version-packages
          publish: npm run publish:changesets
          commit: "release: version packages"
          title: "release: version packages"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

2

4	
5	---
6	
7	## Problem: file: links are not a release boundary
8	
9	Every runtime currently resolves fork packages via `file:` links in `my-pi` root `devDependencies`:
10	
11	```
12	"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent"
13	"@earendil-works/pi-agent-core":   "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/agent"
14	"@earendil-works/pi-ai":           "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/ai"
15	"@earendil-works/pi-tui":          "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/tui"
16	```
17	
18	Consequence: `npm install` on a pod or action runner resolves to whatever the filesystem has at build time. Two builds from the same commit can produce different binaries if the fork checkout differs. Rollback is "re-checkout the fork at some commit and rebuild" — fragile, undocumented, invisible.
19	
20	The fix is a **versioned registry seam**: publish fork packages and extension/profile packages to a scoped registry; each runtime pins a profile version; rollback = redeploy the previous tag.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Update flow
25	
26	There are two update lanes; keep them separate:
27	
28	- **Upstream Pi release available** (startup banner says `New version X is available. Run pi update`): for Luke's source/fork install, run `pi update` only if `settings.sourceUpdateCommand` points at `~/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent`; otherwise run `~/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi`. This creates/uses an update branch, merges/rebases upstream into `pi-mono-fork`, runs the fork gate, then refreshes extensions with `pi update --extensions`.
29	- **Extension/package update available**: run `pi update --extensions` (or `pi update npm:<package>` for one package). This updates installed Pi packages/extensions only; it does not replace the fork checkout or binary.
30	
31	Fork versions use `0.78.0-luke.N`. The startup version checker should not nag when upstream latest is the same base `0.78.0`; it should nag again when upstream publishes a higher base such as `0.78.1`.
32	
33	## Registry
34	
35	**Primary**: GitHub Packages, scope `@valkyriweb`.
36	- Auth: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` = GitHub PAT with `packages:write`. Already available in the `valkyriweb` org.
37	- Registry URL: `https://npm.pkg.github.com`
38	- `.npmrc` in fork root and `my-pi` root: `@valkyriweb:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`
39	
40	**Alternate for offline pods**: Verdaccio on `lue-kube` (self-hosted in-cluster registry/proxy that caches `@valkyriweb/*` + public deps). **Decision (2026-05-30): GitHub Packages is primary/source-of-truth; Verdaccio is deferred** — do NOT stand it up until a concrete trigger: (a) a pod/runtime that genuinely cannot reach github.com, (b) GH Packages egress/auth/rate-limit pain once the fleet pulls heavily, or (c) builds must survive a GitHub outage. Until then GH Packages alone is simpler and sufficient. When stood up, track in `docs/pi-stack-inventory.md`.
41	
42	During development (laptop only): `file:` links remain in place. Kill file: links only for release builds — see "Kill file: links" below.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Three release layers
47	
48	### Layer 1 — Fork packages (upstream baseline + platform delta)
49	
50	Packages currently needed by the fork: `@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent`, `@valkyriweb/pi-agent-core`, `@valkyriweb/pi-ai`, `@valkyriweb/pi-tui`.
51	
52	**Maintenance policy: upstream by default.** Do **not** publish/control an upstream-maintained support package unless it carries real fork delta required by the coding-agent runtime. If a package has zero fork delta — or its delta is upstreamed/retired — switch that dependency back to the upstream `@earendil-works/*` package and remove the `@valkyriweb` copy from the release set. The only product lifecycle we own is the forked coding-agent runtime; support packages are private, lockstep implementation detail while they differ from upstream.
53	
54	These are the `@earendil-works/*` fork packages republished under the `@valkyriweb` scope only while needed. Their SemVer version encodes the upstream baseline + the platform-delta commits on top.
55	
56	Version scheme: `<upstream-version>-luke.<N>` e.g. `0.78.0-luke.3`. Patch bump on each fork-delta release. Major/minor track upstream. Keep support packages lockstep with the CLI; do not give them independent product roadmaps.
57	
58	Add `publishConfig` to each fork `package.json`:
59	```json
60	"publishConfig": { "registry": "https://npm.pkg.github.com", "access": "restricted" }
61	```
62	
63	### Layer 2 — Extensions + profile manifests
64	
65	Each extension under `my-pi/extensions/` and each profile manifest under `my-pi/packages/` becomes its own versioned package with a `peerDependency` on the Layer 1 fork range:
66	
67	```json
68	"peerDependencies": {
69	  "@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.79.0"
70	}
71	```
72	
73	Published as e.g. `@valkyriweb/pi-native-tool-overrides`, `@valkyriweb/my-pi-full`.
74	
75	A profile manifest `package.json` declares `dependencies` on the exact extension versions it bundles — this is the "what runs here" bill of materials. Pi package loading does **not** automatically compose sibling packages after npm install: dependent pi packages must be in `dependencies` + `bundledDependencies`, and profile `pi.extensions` paths must reference bundled `node_modules/...` resources (per `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/packages.md`). Generate release-shaped profile manifests with `npm run profiles:release-manifests`; output goes to ignored `.release/profile-manifests/` for inspection/packaging.
76	
77	### Layer 3 — Per-runtime lockfile pin
78	
79	Each runtime (laptop, openclaw, pod, clawsweeper) pins a single profile version in its `package.json` or deployment manifest:
80	
81	```json
82	"dependencies": {
83	  "@valkyriweb/my-pi-full": "1.4.2"
84	}
85	```
86	
87	`npm ci` against the lockfile produces a reproducible image. "What runs here" is one version number.
88	
89	Pod/clawsweeper: build image with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, bake into the container image layer. Rollback = redeploy the container image tagged at the previous profile version.
90	
91	---
92	
93	## Tooling: Changesets
94	
95	Use `@changesets/cli` for the release flow. Do not hand-bump versions.
96	
97	OpenClaw-style boundary: Changesets is the release mechanism, not the PR-time reviewer. The official Changesets GitHub App should not be installed as a PR nag bot for this repo; it races smarter guards and creates email noise. PR-time missing-changeset decisions belong in trusted-base CI/ClawSweeper review. The only Changesets "bot" path we want is the checked-in release workflow that versions and publishes.
98	
99	**Current state (2026-06-01): the auto-PR release loop is WIRED in both repos.** `my-pi/.github/workflows/release.yml` and `pi-mono-fork/.github/workflows/release.yml` both run a blocking stability gate, then `changesets/action@v1` (`version` + `publish`). On a push to `main` with pending changesets the action opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR; **merging that PR is a deliberate manual approval step** (gotcha #7), and the merge commit's push to `main` re-triggers the workflow, which then publishes + tags. Both workflows also expose `workflow_dispatch` for manual re-trigger. We intentionally do NOT auto-merge the Version PR (unlike upstream `howaboua-pi-stuff`) — publish stays human-gated.
100	
101	The manual runbook below remains valid as a fallback / for off-CI releases.
102	
103	Config: `.changeset/config.json` in both `pi-mono-fork` and `my-pi` roots. Both use `@changesets/changelog-github` (`{ "repo": "valkyriweb/<repo>" }`) so changelog entries carry PR + author links; this needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` at `changeset version` time (CI provides it; locally `export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)`).
104	
105	### Composed version + aggregate + rollup (my-pi)
106	
107	`my-pi`'s `version-packages` script is composed, not bare `changeset version`:
108	
109	```
110	node scripts/add-aggregate-changesets.mjs    # auto-bump profiles whose members changed
111	&& changeset version                         # consume changesets -> bump versions + CHANGELOGs
112	&& node scripts/sync-monorepo-changelog.mjs  # roll latest per-package sections into root CHANGELOG.md
113	```
114	
115	- **`add-aggregate-changesets.mjs`** (`npm run changeset:aggregates`): profile packages (`@valkyriweb/my-pi-*`) bundle member extensions at pinned versions. When a member gets a changeset, this writes a generated `.changeset/aggregate-profiles.md` patch-bumping every profile that bundles it, so a runtime pinning a profile version actually receives the member update. The file is git-ignored and consumed by the immediately-following `changeset version`.
116	- **`sync-monorepo-changelog.mjs`** (`npm run changelog:sync`): regenerates everything below the `<!-- package-changelog-summary -->` marker in the root `CHANGELOG.md` from each released package's latest section. Hand-written intro above the marker is preserved.
117

119	
120	Profiles bundle their members so a runtime can `npm install @valkyriweb/my-pi-<x>` and get a working profile + all extensions. The source manifest is dev-shaped (no `dependencies`, `pi.extensions` as relative `../../<area>/<member>/...` paths), so it is **not** publishable as-is. `scripts/build-profile-release-manifests.mjs` transforms a profile to release shape:

# Release Engineering

read_when: setting up versioned builds; landing a change to any fork package or extension; debugging non-reproducible pod/clawsweeper images; wiring cache/prompt-stability gates into CI; rolling back a runtime to a known-good version.

---

## Problem: file: links are not a release boundary

Every runtime currently resolves fork packages via `file:` links in `my-pi` root `devDependencies`:

```
"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent"
"@earendil-works/pi-agent-core":   "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/agent"
"@earendil-works/pi-ai":           "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/ai"
"@earendil-works/pi-tui":          "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/tui"
```

Consequence: `npm install` on a pod or action runner resolves to whatever the filesystem has at build time. Two builds from the same commit can produce different binaries if the fork checkout differs. Rollback is "re-checkout the fork at some commit and rebuild" — fragile, undocumented, invisible.

The fix is a **versioned registry seam**: publish fork packages and extension/profile packages to a scoped registry; each runtime pins a profile version; rollback = redeploy the previous tag.

---

## Update flow

There are two update lanes; keep them separate:

- **Upstream Pi release available** (startup banner says `New version X is available. Run pi update`): for Luke's source/fork install, run `pi update` only if `settings.sourceUpdateCommand` points at `~/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent`; otherwise run `~/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi`. This creates/uses an update branch, merges/rebases upstream into `pi-mono-fork`, runs the fork gate, then refreshes extensions with `pi update --extensions`.
- **Extension/package update available**: run `pi update --extensions` (or `pi update npm:<package>` for one package). This updates installed Pi packages/extensions only; it does not replace the fork checkout or binary.

Fork versions use `0.78.0-luke.N`. The startup version checker should not nag when upstream latest is the same base `0.78.0`; it should nag again when upstream publishes a higher base such as `0.78.1`.

## Registry

**Primary**: GitHub Packages, scope `@valkyriweb`.
- Auth: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` = GitHub PAT with `packages:write`. Already available in the `valkyriweb` org.
- Registry URL: `https://npm.pkg.github.com`
- `.npmrc` in fork root and `my-pi` root: `@valkyriweb:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`

**Alternate for offline pods**: Verdaccio on `lue-kube` (self-hosted in-cluster registry/proxy that caches `@valkyriweb/*` + public deps). **Decision (2026-05-30): GitHub Packages is primary/source-of-truth; Verdaccio is deferred** — do NOT stand it up until a concrete trigger: (a) a pod/runtime that genuinely cannot reach github.com, (b) GH Packages egress/auth/rate-limit pain once the fleet pulls heavily, or (c) builds must survive a GitHub outage. Until then GH Packages alone is simpler and sufficient. When stood up, track in `docs/pi-stack-inventory.md`.

During development (laptop only): `file:` links remain in place. Kill file: links only for release builds — see "Kill file: links" below.

---

## Three release layers

### Layer 1 — Fork packages (upstream baseline + platform delta)

Packages currently needed by the fork: `@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent`, `@valkyriweb/pi-agent-core`, `@valkyriweb/pi-ai`, `@valkyriweb/pi-tui`.

**Maintenance policy: upstream by default.** Do **not** publish/control an upstream-maintained support package unless it carries real fork delta required by the coding-agent runtime. If a package has zero fork delta — or its delta is upstreamed/retired — switch that dependency back to the upstream `@earendil-works/*` package and remove the `@valkyriweb` copy from the release set. The only product lifecycle we own is the forked coding-agent runtime; support packages are private, lockstep implementation detail while they differ from upstream.

These are the `@earendil-works/*` fork packages republished under the `@valkyriweb` scope only while needed. Their SemVer version encodes the upstream baseline + the platform-delta commits on top.

Version scheme: `<upstream-version>-luke.<N>` e.g. `0.78.0-luke.3`. Patch bump on each fork-delta release. Major/minor track upstream. Keep support packages lockstep with the CLI; do not give them independent product roadmaps.

Add `publishConfig` to each fork `package.json`:
```json
"publishConfig": { "registry": "https://npm.pkg.github.com", "access": "restricted" }
```

### Layer 2 — Extensions + profile manifests

Each extension under `my-pi/extensions/` and each profile manifest under `my-pi/packages/` becomes its own versioned package with a `peerDependency` on the Layer 1 fork range:

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.79.0"
}
```

Published as e.g. `@valkyriweb/pi-native-tool-overrides`, `@valkyriweb/my-pi-full`.

A profile manifest `package.json` declares `dependencies` on the exact extension versions it bundles — this is the "what runs here" bill of materials. Pi package loading does **not** automatically compose sibling packages after npm install: dependent pi packages must be in `dependencies` + `bundledDependencies`, and profile `pi.extensions` paths must reference bundled `node_modules/...` resources (per `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/packages.md`). Generate release-shaped profile manifests with `npm run profiles:release-manifests`; output goes to ignored `.release/profile-manifests/` for inspection/packaging.

### Layer 3 — Per-runtime lockfile pin

Each runtime (laptop, openclaw, pod, clawsweeper) pins a single profile version in its `package.json` or deployment manifest:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@valkyriweb/my-pi-full": "1.4.2"
}
```

`npm ci` against the lockfile produces a reproducible image. "What runs here" is one version number.

Pod/clawsweeper: build image with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, bake into the container image layer. Rollback = redeploy the container image tagged at the previous profile version.

---

## Tooling: Changesets

Use `@changesets/cli` for the release flow. Do not hand-bump versions.

OpenClaw-style boundary: Changesets is the release mechanism, not the PR-time reviewer. The official Changesets GitHub App should not be installed as a PR nag bot for this repo; it races smarter guards and creates email noise. PR-time missing-changeset decisions belong in trusted-base CI/ClawSweeper review. The only Changesets "bot" path we want is the checked-in release workflow that versions and publishes.

**Current state (2026-06-01): the auto-PR release loop is WIRED in both repos.** `my-pi/.github/workflows/release.yml` and `pi-mono-fork/.github/workflows/release.yml` both run a blocking stability gate, then `changesets/action@v1` (`version` + `publish`). On a push to `main` with pending changesets the action opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR; **merging that PR is a deliberate manual approval step** (gotcha #7), and the merge commit's push to `main` re-triggers the workflow, which then publishes + tags. Both workflows also expose `workflow_dispatch` for manual re-trigger. We intentionally do NOT auto-merge the Version PR (unlike upstream `howaboua-pi-stuff`) — publish stays human-gated.

The manual runbook below remains valid as a fallback / for off-CI releases.

Config: `.changeset/config.json` in both `pi-mono-fork` and `my-pi` roots. Both use `@changesets/changelog-github` (`{ "repo": "valkyriweb/<repo>" }`) so changelog entries carry PR + author links; this needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` at `changeset version` time (CI provides it; locally `export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)`).

### Composed version + aggregate + rollup (my-pi)

`my-pi`'s `version-packages` script is composed, not bare `changeset version`:

```
node scripts/add-aggregate-changesets.mjs    # auto-bump profiles whose members changed
&& changeset version                         # consume changesets -> bump versions + CHANGELOGs
&& node scripts/sync-monorepo-changelog.mjs  # roll latest per-package sections into root CHANGELOG.md
```

- **`add-aggregate-changesets.mjs`** (`npm run changeset:aggregates`): profile packages (`@valkyriweb/my-pi-*`) bundle member extensions at pinned versions. When a member gets a changeset, this writes a generated `.changeset/aggregate-profiles.md` patch-bumping every profile that bundles it, so a runtime pinning a profile version actually receives the member update. The file is git-ignored and consumed by the immediately-following `changeset version`.
- **`sync-monorepo-changelog.mjs`** (`npm run changelog:sync`): regenerates everything below the `<!-- package-changelog-summary -->` marker in the root `CHANGELOG.md` from each released package's latest section. Hand-written intro above the marker is preserved.

### Profile publishability gate (2026-06-01)

Profiles bundle their members so a runtime can `npm install @valkyriweb/my-pi-<x>` and get a working profile + all extensions. The source manifest is dev-shaped (no `dependencies`, `pi.extensions` as relative `../../<area>/<member>/...` paths), so it is **not** publishable as-is. `scripts/build-profile-release-manifests.mjs` transforms a profile to release shape:

content.content:
120	Profiles bundle their members so a runtime can `npm install @valkyriweb/my-pi-<x>` and get a working profile + all extensions. The source manifest is dev-shaped (no `dependencies`, `pi.extensions` as relative `../../<area>/<member>/...` paths), so it is **not** publishable as-is. `scripts/build-profile-release-manifests.mjs` transforms a profile to release shape:
121	
122	- workspace members (`@valkyriweb/*`, plus the vendored `@howaboua/pi-semantic-grep`) → `bundledDependencies`, staged as **real files** into `packages/<profile>/node_modules/<name>/` (the workspace symlinks are dereferenced; npm does not bundle symlinks).
123	- members' external runtime deps (`opik`, `effect`, `better-sqlite3`, `@opentelemetry/*`, …) → hoisted into the profile's `dependencies` so the consumer installs them from the registry. **Native modules stay registry deps, never bundled** — they must rebuild per consumer platform.
124	- members' `peerDependencies` (the 4 pi host packages: `pi-coding-agent`/`pi-agent-core`/`pi-ai`/`pi-tui`) → hoisted to the profile's `peerDependencies` (host-provided, not installed).
125	- `pi.extensions` paths rewritten to `node_modules/<name>/...`.
126	
127	Modes: default → write to ignored `.release/profile-manifests/` for inspection; `--in-place` → rewrite `packages/<profile>/package.json` (backed up to `.orig`) **and** stage member files into `node_modules/`; `--restore` → restore the manifest from `.orig` and remove the staged `node_modules/`; `--include-private` → also process private profiles (default `--in-place` skips them). Exposed as `npm run profiles:release-{prep,restore}`.
128	
129	`publish:changesets` is `profiles:release-prep && changeset publish && profiles:release-restore`. `release-prep` skips private profiles, so while the gate is on it is a clean no-op and `changeset publish` ships only the non-private packages (e.g. `pi-memory`). The rewritten manifests + staged `node_modules/` are transient and never committed (`.orig` and `node_modules/` are git-ignored).
130	
131	**Status (validated 2026-06-01):** the mechanism works. `npm run profiles:release-prep -- --include-private` then `npm pack --dry-run` shows every bundled member's files in the tarball (my-pi-pod: pi-observability + hoisted `opik`; my-pi-full: all 36 members, 17 hoisted external deps, ~8 MB unpacked). `profiles:release-restore` leaves the tree clean (manifests match HEAD, no `node_modules/`/`.orig`).
132	
133	**Go-live (2026-06-01): the 4 profiles were flipped to `private: false`.** They were gated `private: true` only while the bundling mechanism was being built + validated — not because publishing them is dangerous. With the mechanism proven, the gate came off. `release-prep` now stages them, and the next publish run ships the bundled tarballs.
134	
135	### What "publishing a profile" actually does (read this before worrying)
136	
137	Three separate things that are easy to conflate. Flipping `private` touches only the first.
138	
139	1. **`private` (in `package.json`) = the npm publish switch, nothing else.** `true` = "npm, refuse to publish this." `false` (or absent) = "npm, you may publish this." It has **zero** effect on the GitHub *repository* — `my-pi` stays exactly as visible as it is. It does not make code public.
140	
141	2. **Where a published profile goes = a private, org-scoped registry.** Both the profile's `publishConfig` and `.changeset/config.json` pin `registry: https://npm.pkg.github.com` (GitHub Packages) + `access: restricted`, and `.npmrc` routes the `@valkyriweb` scope there behind `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. So a published profile is an **org-private package**: you need a GitHub token with `@valkyriweb` org access just to `npm install` it. **Nothing is published to public npmjs.com.** Package visibility follows the org/repo; making a GitHub Package truly public is a separate, explicit action in GitHub Packages settings.
142	
143	3. **What triggers an actual publish = a push to `main` with no pending changesets.** `release.yml` runs on every push but only acts when there is release work (see its header). Two cases:
144	   - **changesets present** → it opens/updates the "Version Packages" PR (bumps versions + CHANGELOGs). **No publish.** This is the human gate — publishing waits for you to merge that PR.
145	   - **no changesets present** (e.g. right after the Version PR merged) → it runs `publish:changesets`, which publishes any non-`private` package whose version isn't on the registry yet, and pushes git tags.
146

#!/bin/bash
# Versioned registry install of pi 0.78.3 + my-pi-full 0.1.9 on the Mac Mini (Layer 3 pin).
set -euo pipefail

NODE24="$HOME/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v24.14.0/installation/bin"
export PATH="$NODE24:$PATH"

DIR="$HOME/.local/share/pi/v0.78.3-registry"
mkdir -p "$DIR"
cd "$DIR"

printf '@valkyriweb:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}\n' > .npmrc

cat > package.json <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "pi-runtime-mac-mini",
  "private": true,
  "description": "Layer-3 pin: versioned pi runtime + profile for luke-and-naddy-server",
  "dependencies": {
    "@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": "0.78.3",
    "@valkyriweb/my-pi-full": "0.1.9"
  }
}
EOF

NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) npm install --no-audit --no-fund

cat > pi-wrapper.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
export PATH="$NODE24:\$PATH"
exec node "$DIR/node_modules/@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent/dist/cli.js" "\$@"
EOF
chmod +x pi-wrapper.sh

ln -sf "$DIR/pi-wrapper.sh" "$HOME/.local/bin/pi"

mkdir -p "$HOME/.pi/agent"
if [ ! -f "$HOME/.pi/agent/settings.json" ]; then
  cat > "$HOME/.pi/agent/settings.json" <<EOF
{
  "packages": [
    "$DIR/node_modules/@valkyriweb/my-pi-full"
  ]
}
EOF
fi

echo "--- smoke ---"
"$HOME/.local/bin/pi" --version

9	  // deferred-tools list incl. the consented Workflow tool (~1.5k), and the
10	  // session-stable available_skills routing index (~21kB ≈ 5.3k tokens). Was
11	  // 30_000 — sized before the Workflow tool joined the profile and before the
12	  // skills byte budget was raised 8k→28k (a2b9145), which together push the
13	  // healthy baseline just over 30k. Raised to 33_000 (≈2k headroom over the
14	  // observed peak) 2026-05-29. Rebaselined narrowly to 34_000 on 2026-05-30
15	  // after the live prompt landed at 33.5k with no duplicate tools or skill leaks;
16	  // still catches a real ~10% bloat regression.
17	  maxTotalPromptTokens: 34_000,
18	  // 15 since 2026-05-30: + EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode (pi-mode, WS13) are eager
19	  // for CC parity — the model calls them directly to enter plan mode and to
20	  // request approval to exit (CC's plan tools are always available, not

22	  // WS9), 12 before that.
23	  maxEagerTools: 15,
24	  maxActiveTools: 40,
25	  // available_skills is the cached, session-stable parent-skill routing index
26	  // (children defer under parents via skill_search). Trigger-rich descriptions
27	  // are load-bearing for routing, not fat — a healthy ~26-parent install is
28	  // ~21 kB. Budget catches real regressions: child-deferral breaking (~56

30	  // check). Was 8_000 (sized for a far smaller install); raised 2026-05-29.

# Pi Development — Router

## Core rule

- Customize Pi via `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` extensions/packages first.
- Patch `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` core only for generic platform primitives that cannot be exposed through existing hooks/filters.
- If core changes are unavoidable, log them in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run the fork + extension gates.

## Read when

| Work | Read |
|---|---|
| Any Pi extension/package/fork implementation | `~/Projects/agent-scripts/references/pi-dev-details.md` |
| Prompt-cache, `tools[]`, system prompt, `forkAgent`, child agents, memory extractors | skill `pi-cache-stability` + `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` |
| Extension API / examples | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md` |
| Runtime/package inventory | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |
| Setup/runtime registry changes | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` catalog YAML; generated files are scanner-owned |
| Config settings / env layering | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/config-layering.md` |
| Release/versioning/rollback | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` |

## Hot paths

- Core fork: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (`packages/coding-agent` for agent loop/tools/docs).
- Extension lab: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/`.
- Full profile: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/packages/my-pi-full/package.json`.
- Claude bridge: `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` at `http://127.0.0.1:9100`.
- Model metadata: `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; Opus 4.8 is `claude-bridge/claude-opus-4-8`.

## Cache footguns

- Keep `params.system` and `tools[]` byte-stable across same-cwd sessions.
- Put dynamic recall/time/status/session data in appended messages/tool results, not cached system-prefix text.
- Mark situational/heavy extension tools `deferLoading: true`; gate with `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:deferred-tool-contracts`.
- Guard `setActiveTools`: call only when the normalized tool-name set changes.
- Prefer `tool_reference` / provider-native `defer_loading` over mutating active tools after `tool_search`.

## Gates

- Extension/profile/cache surface: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`.
- Fork/core surface: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.
- Native aliases: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.
- Prompt-health probe: `pi-prompt-health --refresh`, send one Pi message, then `pi-prompt-health`.

# How I Work

Use progressive disclosure where possible for context efficiency, see progressive-disclosure skill

Tradeoff: These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

1. Think Before Coding
Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.

Before implementing:

State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
2. Simplicity First
Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.

Good code should read like a clear action sequence:

```ts
const harness = await init({ model });
const session = await harness.session();
const result = await session.prompt(prompt, { schema });
```

```php
Route::resource('photos', PhotoController::class)
    ->only(['index', 'show']);

Flight::where('active', 1)
    ->orderBy('name')
    ->limit(10)
    ->get();
```

No features beyond what was asked.
No abstractions for single-use code.
No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
No error handling for impossible scenarios.
If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

3. Surgical Changes
Touch only what you must. Quality improvements stay inside the task's boundary.

Reuse before adding:

Reuse existing types, utilities, hooks, components, and patterns before writing new ones.
Don't broaden public APIs unless the acceptance criteria require it.

When editing existing code:

Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When quality blocks the task:

If confusing, duplicated, or hard-to-test code blocks a clean implementation, improve that code as part of the change.
If a small local cleanup makes the implementation simpler or safer, do it and call it out (PR body / summary).
A real quality issue not needed for the change → flag it for follow-up; don't expand scope.

When your changes create orphans:
Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

4. Goal-Driven Execution
Define success criteria. Loop until verified.

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

"Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
"Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
"Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

For spec-backed work:
- Keep each slice traceable to a spec section, issue, or acceptance bullet.
- Answer "what's left?" with concrete file/task deltas, not broad themes.
- After risky or architecture-heavy slices, report done, yet-to-do, spec deviations, roadblocks, and harder-than-expected parts.
- Treat review feedback as a loop: implement slice → inspect diff/comments → fix → promote repeated style feedback into AGENTS.md or the relevant skill.
- Checkpoint completed slices before starting a risky refactor.
- For gnarly threads, write a short handoff that links existing specs/artifacts instead of duplicating them.

These guidelines are working if: fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

Don’t fight errors: after the same error twice, stop and gather new evidence — local docs/source first, then web if version/API behavior is unclear — before choosing a fix.

# SOUL.md — Rusty

## Core

**Just answer.** Never open with "Great question", "I'd be happy to help", or "Absolutely". Just answer.

**Brevity is mandatory.** If the answer fits in one sentence, one sentence is what Luke gets. Long replies are a tax; charge only when worth it.

**Have opinions. Strong ones.** Stop hiding behind "it depends". Pick the best path, say why, move.

**Do the obvious work.** Reversible, local, boring? Do it. Ask only for destructive, external, private, or genuinely ambiguous moves.

**Use tools before asking.** Read the file. Check the log. Grep the repo. Come back with answers, not vibes.

**Call out bad ideas early.** If Luke is about to footgun himself, say so. Charm over cruelty, but don't sugarcoat.

**Keep private private.** Don't leak Luke's stuff. Don't act as Luke in public without a clear go-ahead. No PII in github.

## Voice

- Sharp, warm, terse.
- Opinionated without being a dick.
- Funny when it happens naturally. No forced jokes.
- Swearing is allowed when it lands. A real "holy shit" beats five sterile adjectives. Don't overdo it.
- Telegraph style. Drop filler. Match Luke's pace.
- Praise only when earned. If something is fucking brilliant, say so.

## Vibe

Smart friend at the desk. Calm under pressure. Dry wit. Clean takes. No corporate mist. No sycophant sludge.

Be the assistant you'd actually want to talk to at 2am. Not a corporate drone. Not a sycophant. Just... good.

## Continuity

These files are memory. Read them. Update them when Luke asks or when a real preference becomes obvious.

If you change this file, tell Luke.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
